items.title: Talayuela, el pueblo de Cáceres que se queda sin profesores de árabe
items.description: Los alumnos del pueblo cacereño de Talayuela ya no contarán con los dos maestros que tradicionalmente llegaban de Marruecos para ofrecer clases de árabe. El acuerdo de gobierno que alcanzaron el PP y Vox en Extremadura prometía acabar con ese programa este mismo año, pero la comunidad educativa se movilizó para que continuara. No ha podido ser. En un intento por sortear las intenciones de Vox, los dos colegios de Talayuela, los únicos en Extremadura que se habían acogido al programa dada su alta población de alumnos de origen marroquí, alcanzaron un acuerdo con la Consejería de Educación regional y con el Ayuntamiento, también gobernado por el PP y Vox, para buscar una solución. La encontraron sacando del centro escolar las clases de árabe, que se impartirían en unas aulas prestadas por la localidad, pero el Ministerio de Educación no acepta ese arreglo porque “el convenio contempla que esas actividades y su inspección educativa solo se pueden producir en los centros docentes”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Mazón regresa al Congreso para responder de nuevo sobre su papel en la gestión de la dana
items.description: El expresident Carles Mazón acude este lunes a las 11.00 al Congreso para afrontar de nuevo las preguntas de la comisión de investigación sobre la gestión de la crisis derivada de la dana, que causó 232 fallecidos a consecuencia de las inundaciones del 29 de octubre de 2024. Y lo hace tan solo cuatro días después de que la Fiscalía del Tribunal Supremo solicitara el auto del Tribunal Superior de Justicia de la Comunitat Valenciana sobre él ―en el que le exculpó de toda responsabilidad de la tragedia― para evaluar la querella que interpusieron contra él cuatro diputados socialistas por falso testimonio durante su primera visita en la comisión de investigación del Congreso. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los venezolanos se autocensuran ante el poder de Estados Unidos: “Ahora no sé si debo temer a la CIA”
items.description: La frase es exagerada, pero transmite una sensación compartida: “ Antes tenía miedo del Sebin [Servicio Bolivariano de Inteligencia Nacional] y ahora no sé si tengo que temer a la CIA”. La pronuncia un diputado opositor una calurosa mañana de septiembre en Caracas y refleja un temor creciente entre políticos, periodistas, empresarios y defensores de los derechos humanos. El poder de Estados Unidos en Venezuela y su respaldo al Gobierno de Delcy Rodríguez los mantiene desconcertados y cuidadosos. Cuando la represión por decir lo que uno piensa empezaba a disiparse, surge un nuevo miedo: contrariar los intereses de la primera potencia mundial. En juego hay visados, financiación de proyectos y la condena al ostracismo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Europa se plantea garantizar a las grandes compañías de IA el acceso total a los datos de los ciudadanos
items.description: La presidencia irlandesa de la UE propondrá a los Estados miembros que el uso de los datos “en el contexto de la inteligencia artificial (IA)” sea automáticamente legal. Eso permitiría a las desarrolladoras de IA, como OpenAI, Anthropic, Google o Meta, usar toda la información que hayan recopilado en los últimos años (o décadas, en el caso de Google y Meta) para entrenar sus modelos. Eso se desprende de un documento oficial de Dublín, conseguido por la organización Noyb y al que ha tenido acceso EL PAÍS, en el que se recoge la propuesta de modificación del Reglamento General de Protección de Datos (RGPD), la norma que defiende el derecho fundamental a la privacidad de los ciudadanos europeos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Oficina del sheriff, ‘saloon’ y horca: se vende poblado del Oeste en Almería
items.description: A finales de los años 60, el italiano Sergio Leone aterrizó en la provincia de Almería para rodar la película Hasta que llegó su hora . Alucinó con el paisaje, pero el desierto no bastaba: su equipo de producción levantó un decorado diseñado por Carlo Simi que incluía varios edificios y un ferrocarril. Fue bautizado como Rancho Leone y acogió desde entonces otros muchos rodajes de los míticos spaghetti western , pero también series, videoclips o campañas publicitarias. Pedro Almodóvar también pasó por allí en 2023 para rodar Extraña forma de vida con Ethan Hawke y Pedro Pascal. Hoy, este escenario, en decadencia por su escaso mantenimiento, está a la venta por 1,6 millones de euros. “Estamos ya mayores, cansados. Tuvo una época buenísima, pero ya no podemos con todo esto”, cuenta a la entrada de las instalaciones Genara Rubio, gerente y propietaria del espacio. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Groenlandia no es de Trump
items.description: Donald Trump ya puede recurrir tanto como quiera a la retórica grandilocuente y difundir en sus redes mapas con el continente americano teñido de las barras y estrellas. Los hechos son tozudos y al final tendrá que aceptarlos: Groenlandia pertenece al Reino de Dinamarca. El presidente estadounidense ha proclamado que el acuerdo anunciado este fin de semana con Copenhague y Nuuk , la capital groenlandesa, dará a su país “un control permanente sobre sus necesidades en seguridad y sobre todas las otras necesidades”. Lo ha celebrado como un triunfo. La realidad es que la primera potencia mundial tenía garantizada desde hacía décadas esta presencia militar en el territorio ártico y no existía ningún obstáculo para ampliarla si lo deseaba. Y, sobre todo: queda preservado lo esencial, que era el respeto a la soberanía y la integridad territorial. Trump había intentado destruirlas. Hoy da marcha atrás, a tenor de los detalles que se han conocido sobre el documento que debe firmarse esta semana durante la Asamblea General de la ONU. El problema creado al provocar con sus amenazas una crisis inédita en la OTAN está en vías de resolverse . Es un éxito de la diplomacia danesa, pero frágil y provisional: nada asegura que el inquilino de la Casa Blanca no vuelva a las andadas. Seguir leyendo

Sus nombres están inscritos en las lápidas de un vasto cementerio, algunas de ellas sobresalientes, otras perdidas entre la hierba. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La jornada de 35 horas avanza en la administración autonómica y local y anticipa conflictos donde aún no se ha implantado
items.description: El Gobierno aprobó el 15 de abril la jornada de 35 horas semanales para los 250.000 trabajadores que tiene la Administración General del Estado (AGE). Ese nuevo escenario en la Administración central esperanzó a los funcionarios de entidades locales y autonómicas —la mayoría de los más de tres millones de empleados públicos que existen en España— que aún no tienen esa jornada: lo veían como un argumento irrebatible en sus mesas de negociación. Y, efectivamente, esa novedad ha agitado las conversaciones y su aplicación en algunos territorios. En otros, donde aún siguen esperando, han amenazado con movilizaciones e incluso con paros si sus reclamaciones no son atendidas. Seguir leyendo ¿Y en el Ejército? El acuerdo que reduce la jornada en la Administración General del Estado de 37 horas y media a 35 no es de aplicación para el Ejército. Tampoco para la Policía Nacional y la Guardia Civil. Todos ellos, unos 284.000 trabajadores, "se encuentran sujetos a su normativa específica", según detalla el Ministerio de Defensa. El departamento de Margarita Robles indica que está tramitando una modificación específica para que los empleados en las Fuerzas Armadas (123.500 de esos 284.000) sí accedan a las 35 horas. De momento, se encuentra en fase de tramitación.

items.title: La generación que dejó de cenar: qué pasa con los trastornos alimenticios en mujeres mayores de 50
items.description: Un grupo de amigas de mediana edad quedan por la noche “para tomar algo”. En un momento dado alguna integrante del grupo decide que es hora de picar algo. La cena se convierte en un cuenco de mejillones y un plato de cecina para seis. Aún así, las tapas no se terminan. La escena es habitual entre las mujeres ‘boomers’, especialmente en verano: o no cenan, o el picoteo es tan escaso que lo que a priori el camarero aconseja para dos se reparte entre seis. ¿Es normal que mujeres que han pasado la mediana edad no cenen de forma rutinaria? Seguir leyendo

items.description: María Fitz-James Stuart (Madrid, 51 años) tiene apellido de reyes de Escocia e Inglaterra y título de vizcondesa de Jarafe, pero prefiere que la llamen “la griega”. “Me lo puso una prima y es el apodo más nombre que existe”, dice una de las relaciones públicas más solicitadas de Madrid mientras recorremos su nueva oficina, un espacio diseñado originalmente por Norman Foster. Pasó su infancia como los Durrell , descalza y despreocupada en la isla de Corfú. Cuando volvió a la capital, se sentía una extraña, una extranjera. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las luces y sombras de Gemeliers: “Si hubiéramos cambiado nuestro primer contrato, habríamos sido multimillonarios”
items.description: Jesús y Daniel Oviedo, conocidos artísticamente como Gemeliers , tienen 27 años, pero bromean con que es como si hubieran vivido 50. Antes de cumplir los 18, ya tenían varios discos de platino, dos biografías oficiales publicadas y miles de fans que colapsaban, literalmente, sus firmas de discos —en 2014, en Barcelona, la enorme afluencia de gente bloqueó el tráfico en la Avenida Diagonal y obligó a cancelar el evento por motivos de seguridad pública—. “Yo creo que hacía tiempo que no había en España un nivel de convocatoria como el que teníamos mi hermano y yo. Llevábamos más de 80 personas de equipo de seguridad”, recuerda Jesús. Los hermanos sevillanos recibieron muchísimo cariño, pero también mucho odio. Algo de eso se intuye cuando Daniel comenta riendo que se haría una camiseta con la frase del cartel que acompaña a los distintos instrumentos —un piano, una batería, unos bongos...— que pueblan el hall del Hotel Barceló Imagine de Madrid, donde tiene lugar la entrevista. “Soy muy sensible, por favor, que solo me toquen manos expertas. ¡Gracias por cuidarme!”, señala el letrero. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Cuando Elton John salió del armario hace medio siglo: “¡Lo hubiese dicho antes si alguien me lo hubiese preguntado!"
items.description: “No hay nada malo en acostarse con alguien de tu mismo sexo”. La frase la pronunció Elton John en 1976, en una entrevista para Rolling Stone que se publicó el 7 de octubre de aquel año. Tenía 29 años y estaba en uno de los momentos más grandes de su carrera. No había preparado un comunicado ni estaba intentando convertir su sexualidad en una declaración política. Estaba hablando de sexo, de amor, de la soledad de una vida en la que empezaba a tenerlo todo y no tenía muy claro con quién compartirlo. Y el periodista Cliff Jahr se atrevió a hacerle una pregunta que, según Elton recordaría años después, nadie había tenido “los cojones” de hacerle antes. “Lo hubiese dicho antes si alguien me lo hubiese preguntado”. Y alguien, por fin, se lo había preguntado. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La tienda de pijamas en Roma a la que peregrinan Zendaya, Julianne Moore o Gwyneth Paltrow: “Buscan un poco de normalidad dentro de sus vidas extraordinarias”
items.description: A finales de marzo, Zendaya entró en una pequeña bottega de la Via della Fontanella di Borghese, en el casco histórico de Roma. Esperó su turno y, cuando este llegó, compró un pijama. A decir verdad, se llevó algo más: el pijama de popelín de algodón italiano, con botones de nácar y hecho prácticamente a mano, y, también, “un pequeño paréntesis de normalidad cotidiana dentro de unas vidas que, por lo demás, son extraordinariamente fuera de lo común”. Así lo resume Shirley Bloch, tercera generación al frente de este pequeño negocio, y quien se ha convertido en un nuevo tipo de celebridad entre los famosos. La visita de Zendaya acabó como suelen hacerlo aquí, con un café, charlando sobre perritos, entre pilas y pilas de pijamas estampados. Gwyneth Paltrow, Harry Styles, Bruce Springsteen, Julianne Moore, Dakota Johnson, Mark Ruffalo, Lily Allen, Damiano David, Wes Anderson o Charlotte Gainsbourg han venido hasta aquí a por uno de estos pijamas. También Naomi Campbell, Anne Hathaway, Alessandro Michele: la lista no acaba nunca. Seguir leyendo

items.title: I’m greatly worried – NPA boss on threat of higher transport fares
items.description: The CEO of the National Petroleum Authority (NPA), Godwin Edudzi Tamakloe, says he is “greatly worried” about the prospect of higher transport fares following the latest increase in fuel prices. His concern comes as transport operators push for a fare adjustment, citing rising operational costs. The Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) has maintained its proposal for a 30% increase in transport fares. The latest fuel price increases have added fresh pressure to the ongoing discussions with government. The NPA raised the price floor for petrol to GH¢16 per litre and for diesel to GH¢16.77 per litre from September 16. Some Oil Marketing Companies have since increased their pump prices. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday, Mr Tamakloe said the potential impact of higher fares on consumers and inflation was a major concern. “I’m greatly worried.” He said he and the Transport Minister had been engaging with transport operators to find ways to manage the pressure. “Greatly worried in a sense that together with the Minister for Transport, we’ve been engaging the transport operators, and the whole idea is that government has been doing so well.” Mr Tamakloe said transport operators face several major cost components, including vehicle maintenance, spare parts, fuel, driver and mate payments and insurance. “First of all, for transport business, there are three essential things that you always want to look at: the cost of maintaining the freight, the cost of spare parts. Not only that, the cost of running the business, that’s fuel cost.” He said payments to drivers and mates had generally remained stable, while insurance costs had also largely remained unchanged. “What has become impactful now has to do with the fuel price.” According to him, government measures have helped absorb some of the potential increases transport operators could otherwise have faced. “The cedi stability has absorbed potential cost for you from the forex end. That’s government’s intervention.” He also pointed to government support aimed at cushioning the impact of higher fuel prices. “So the issue now has to do with this. Now government is also coming in to cushion periodically the impact of the increase in prices.” Mr Tamakloe said the NPA and government had engaged transport operators on the need for all sides to share the burden. “So we have jaw-jawed with the various transport owners that there is a time for us to also bear the share.” He said those engagements had helped put the planned fare increase on hold. “And that is why you notice that the attempt to increase the price or increase fares has basically been put on ice.” He commended the leadership of the GPRTU and other transport groups for engaging government constructively. “I think that the GPRTU, and I salute their leadership, the PROTOA and all those other people, that so far we have had some constructive engagement with them, which has greatly been impactful.” However, he said some transport operators had still increased fares without agreement. “There are some a few there are a few recalcitrant ones that have decided to increase their prices arbitrarily.”

items.title: Gernot Döllner, presidente de Audi: “China nos está presionando. Confío en que Europa encuentre soluciones”
items.description: El anuncio del grupo Volkswagen de reducir 50.000 puestos de trabajo extra hasta 2030 (ya había informado de otros 50.000 desde finales de 2024) y recortar su cartera de productos a la mitad ha sido un terremoto que se ha sentido en todo el consorcio alemán. “Audi es parte integral del grupo Volkswagen y tendrá que hacer lo suyo. Desde hace tres años, cuando me incorporé, ya empezamos a hacer la mayor transformación de la historia de Audi ”, señala Gernot Döllner, presidente del consejo de administración de la marca de los cuatro aros, en una entrevista en Madrid. Seguir leyendo La rentabilidad del coche eléctrico Una de las claves del accidentado paso del vehículo de combustión al eléctrico en Europa es la baja rentabilidad del segundo respecto al primero, algo aceptado por el propio Döllner durante esta entrevista, - como también lo hizo el propio Markus Haupt , consejero delegado de Seat y Cupra-. Este último, de hecho, descarta de momento asignar modelos eléctricos a la marca Seat por la escasa rentabilidad que supondría para una firma que de por sí ostenta bajos márgenes, motivo por el que la histórica enseña está en riesgo de desaparecer . "La situación [de la baja rentabilidad del vehículo eléctrico] cambiará a partir de 2030, sobre todo por la regulación de emisiones", indica el presidente de Audi, en referencia a que los límites de emisiones medias para las marcas de las nuevas matriculaciones volverán a endurecerse en ese entonces. "El panorama será distinto. El mensaje positivo es que estamos trabajando intensamente en la próxima generación de vehículos eléctricos, con la que alcanzaremos la paridad de costes, aunque no necesariamente la de beneficios, y eso cambiará las reglas del juego: el coche eléctrico de batería se situará a la par del vehículo de combustión a escala mundial".

items.title: Goods transporters rue seizure of trucks by government
items.description: • Claim sector forms backbone of economy, yet not prioritised by govt; allege HTV licences not being given • Police say regulations for HTV licences in place, 7m violations committed by goods vehicles this year ISLAMABAD: As their vehicles are once again being used to stop protesters from reaching Islamabad, truckers have said the government move has not only “paralysed” the economy but also adds to a litany of their existing grievances. An estimated 400,000 goods vehicles, excluding oil tankers and mini trucks, form the backbone of the logistics network that caters to all major industries and employs millions of people through direct and indirect jobs, they said, adding that despite being a key sector of the economy, they were unfairly treated by the government. They alleged “unfair taxes”, “routine seizure of trucks and containers”, “poor road network”, “excesses by the police and regional transport authorities”, and issues surrounding the HTV licences. The motorway and traffic police denied most of their allegations, including the absence of a proper licensing regime, in separate versions shared with Dawn. It may be noted that goods transporters routinely go on strike to press the government for their demands, most recently in August over daily fuel prices and axle-load limits, among other issues. Their ability to disrupt the entire supply chain often results in the acceptance of their demands, but these remain stopgap measures. All Pakistan Good Transport Owners Association President Imdad Hussain Naqvi said they were the government’s “least priority” despite serving “more than 30 million people every day”. He said their trucks and containers had been seized two weeks before the Sept 27 long march. “This practice has paralysed the country’s economy. The long march will be staged on Sept 27 , but our vehicles and containers were confiscated more than two weeks ago,” he rued. Accompanied by the office-bearers of other associations, Mr Naqvi said that instead of the Ministry of Communications, there must be a separate ministry for transportation. He also said that unless they were given the status of a full-fledged industry, their problems would persist. Mr Naqvi complained that 90 per cent of the truck drivers had LTV driving licences due to an “overly complicated process of converting LTV into HTV licence”, a claim denied by the traffic police. He also talked about the condition of roads across the country, “excessive” taxes and fines, alleged bribes by the regional transport authorities (RTA), and delays in the issuance of provincial route permits. All Pakistan Friends Traders and Trucks/Dumpers Owners Association President Muhammad Rafiq Khan accused weighing stations of overloading trucks in return for heavy bribes. He claimed their letters to the communications ministry remained unanswered. Transport Alliance Chairman Malik Shafaullah Awan said a truck paid Rs35,000 in terms of toll tax from Karachi to Lahore on N-5 (GT Road), besides the petroleum levy on diesel. Police deny allegations Meanwhile, a motorway police spokesperson denied most of the allegations and said the police continued to undertake sustained and effective enforcement measures against Goods Transport Vehicles (GTVs) to ensure compliance with traffic laws and promote road safety. Since January 2026, during the enforcement process, over 7 million traffic violations committed by goods vehicles have been identified, checked and dealt with as per law, the spokesperson said, adding that approximately 692,225 violations related to axle load have been identified and dealt with as per law. There is a proper licensing mechanism for HTVs under the NHMP Drivers Licensing Authority Rules 2014 that specifically prescribe the procedure and eligibility requirements. The National Highways Authority, however, acknowledged the dilapidated state of roads due to the paucity of funds. “We have 14,480 kilometres of roads across Pakistan and the total income NHA fetched through toll was Rs128bn last year; besides, we only get Rs9bn from the government for road maintenance,” NHA General Manager Aftab Badar added. The official said the NHA has to spend its funds on those roads too where it did not get income. “Our 42 per cent of funds are utilised in Balochistan but we received very minimal toll tax from there,” he added. NHA GM (revenue) Ahmed Hassan said NHA denied that any NHA toll plazas were running on an interim basis and added that out of 183 toll plazas, 63 were under the control of Frontier Works Organisation, and 120 were supervised by the NHA. Published in Dawn, September 21st, 2026

items.title: We are largely import-dependent – NPA boss on Ghana’s fuel vulnerability
items.description: The CEO of the National Petroleum Authority (NPA), Godwin Edudzi Tamakloe, says Ghana’s dependence on imported refined petroleum products leaves the country exposed to turbulence whenever external market conditions change. His comments come amid renewed pressure on the downstream petroleum sector as international oil and refined-product prices remain elevated. The NPA has raised its price floor for the second September pricing window, with petrol now pegged at GH¢16 per litre and diesel at GH¢16.77. At the same time, Ghana’s state-owned fuel distributor, BOST, has reduced exports to Burkina Faso and Mali to prioritise domestic supply amid global fuel supply pressures. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday, Mr Tamakloe said he understood from the outset that leading the downstream sector meant dealing with external shocks. “Having to be the Chief Executive Officer of the downstream, I appreciated the fact that we are largely import-dependent when it comes to refined petroleum products.” He said he had therefore always prepared for periods of instability in the industry. “So, I’ve always been, you know, let me say, ready for the potential for turbulence.” According to Mr Tamakloe, Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector is particularly exposed to changes in external factors. “And so it’s been part of the orientation that I’ve had personally, that you are going to, as it were, lead or take charge of an industry that is largely subject to, or, you know, will face turbulence at any time that exogenous or external factors change.” He said the responsibility of leadership is to respond to both favourable and difficult periods. “What I believe is that leadership, in this particular instance, there are issues, and we believe that in a good or bad time, you need to have a leadership response to both sides.” Mr Tamakloe said the NPA has been working to contain the impact of the current turbulence since February. “And so, I would say that we are kind of ready, and from February till now, we’ve been trying to, as it were, manage the turbulence, manage the storm.” He said the Authority’s handling of the situation so far had been satisfactory. “And the management so far has not been bad at all”

items.title: Vessels trickle through Strait of Hormuz as Middle East conflict persists
items.description: By Florence Tan SINGAPORE, Sept 21 (Reuters) - A dozen commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on the weekend, down from 35 the prior weekend, shipping data showed on Monday, as tension in the Gulf persisted with the US and Iran in stalemate. Visible traffic through the strait, the conduit for a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas before the war, has dwindled to a trickle. However, Middle Eastern producers continue to export oil on tankers travelling with their transponders off.

items.title: Ghana’s fuel market is built for turbulence – NPA’s Edudzi Tamakloe explains why
items.description: The CEO of the National Petroleum Authority (NPA), Godwin Edudzi Tamakloe, says Ghana’s dependence on imported refined petroleum products makes turbulence in the fuel market inevitable. He said he assumed leadership of the downstream petroleum sector knowing that external developments could quickly affect the industry. His comments come as Ghana’s fuel market continues to face pressure from developments in the international petroleum market, with changes in global prices being passed through to pump prices. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday, Mr Tamakloe said his role at the NPA required him to be prepared for sudden market changes. “Having to be the Chief Executive Officer of the downstream, I appreciated the fact that we are largely import-dependent when it comes to refined petroleum products.” He said that reality shaped his approach to managing the sector. “So, I’ve always been, you know, let me say, ready for the potential for turbulence.” According to him, Ghana’s petroleum industry is particularly vulnerable to changes in external factors. “And so it’s been part of the orientation that I’ve had personally, that you are going to, as it were, lead or take charge of an industry that is largely subject to, or, you know, will face turbulence at any time that exogenous or external factors change.” Mr Tamakloe said leadership must respond to both favourable and difficult periods in the industry. “What I believe is that leadership, in this particular instance, there are issues, and we believe that in a good or bad time, you need to have a leadership response to both sides.” He said the NPA has been managing the pressures facing the sector since February. “And so, I would say that we are kind of ready, and from February till now, we’ve been trying to, as it were, manage the turbulence, manage the storm.” The NPA boss said the authority’s management of the situation so far has been satisfactory. “And the management so far has not been bad at all.”

items.title: Postponement not an option as Kenya races to be ready for Afcon 2027
items.description: African football boss Patrice Motsepe has called for a “heightened sense of urgency” from next year’s Africa Cup of Nations co-hosts Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. The tournament is set to return to East Africa for the first time in 51 years, with the opening match on 19 June and the final on 17 July. Stadiums are supposed to be ready for testing in around three months’ time, and Confederation of African Football (CAF) president Motsepe says there is little room for delay. “Even though we’ve got nine months, we need to start using those stadiums in January next year to test them and to see what further improvements are required,” he told BBC Sport Africa after inspecting preparations in Kenya on Friday. Motsepe said there had been “very good progress” while also acknowledging that some facilities were still below the required level. “We’ve got very high standards in terms of our expectations of the infrastructure, the facilities and the stadiums, the hotels, the roads, the football pitches where training takes place,” the South African added. “We require those facilities to be world-class.” Despite delays in certain areas, Motsepe insisted: “There isn’t the slightest consideration of a postponement. “There should be no need because there’s a deep amount of commitment.” Kenya to ‘accelerate preparations’ CAF president Patrice Motsepe met Kenyan President William Ruto on his visit to the country on Friday Motsepe began his inspection visit for AFCON 2027 in Tanzania before touring Kenya, where he inspected two venues in Nairobi: Kasarani Stadium and the newly constructed 60,000-capacity Talanta Stadium. BBC Sport Africa understands that one of the main areas of concern in Kenya is Kasarani and its corresponding training facility. The stadium is set to host the 2029 World Athletics Championships, which Nairobi was awarded on Tuesday ahead of London and Rome. When CAF conducted its previous inspection in mid-February, the local organisers were told that stadiums and their associated training facilities should be around 80% ready by August. However, Kasarani has seen limited progress over the past seven months, with several areas still requiring attention. One of the biggest challenges is the playing surface, which is yet to be laid. Work is also required on cabling for broadcast and television operations, floodlights and the stadiums’ sky boxes. Motsepe also pointed to the demands created by hosting hundreds of VIPs and heads of state, saying some stadium designs will need to be reconfigured. “Security issues in relation to where the special guests, particularly the heads of state, will be seated require a revision of the original plans,” the 64-year-old explained. Kenya’s cabinet secretary for sports, Salim Mvurya, insisted that preparations would be completed on time. “I assure CAF and Kenyans we will accelerate the preparations for AFCON 2027,” Mvurya said. “We will conclude everything by December to be sure we can have test matches in the various facilities.” December is significant because Motsepe is due to return to the region for a final assessment visit in January. Recent CAF tournaments have regularly been delayed from their original dates. This year’s Women’s Africa Cup of Nations was played in July after the planned kick-off in March was postponed with just 12 days’ notice. The 2024 African Nations Championship – the former tournament for home-based players only – in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda was postponed from its intended February 2025 dates to August 2025 to ensure infrastructure and facilities were “at the levels necessary”. That decision came 18 days before the tournament was due to start. Meanwhile, the 2023 AFCON in Ivory Coast was moved to early 2024 due to concerns about the rainy season. Two years ago, Motsepe’s former deputy Veron Mosengo-Omba admitted that CAF faced a “scheduling nightmare” to fit its biennial tournaments into the crowded football calendar. Some pundits claim that is part of the reasoning behind the decision to play the men’s Afcon every four years after 2028. Sporting legacy Nairobi’s Kasarani Stadium, which is under renovation, is set to host Africa’s first-ever World Athletics Championships in 2029 Despite previous delays to tournaments and concerns over preparations in East Africa, Motsepe has made it clear the Afcon 2027 timetable will not be reconsidered. “There’s no plan B, there’s no plan C,” he said. For Kenya, getting it right this time matters more because Afcon has become part of a bigger sporting project. “One of the reasons why Kenya won the 2029 World Athletics Championship bid is because we are hosting Afcon. Therefore, this is a legacy,” Mvurya said. “Sport is not just entertainment; it is a livelihood; it is economic transformation. “Therefore, we are aware that the opportunity to host AFCON will be key for our economic inspiration. Our tourism will be a big beneficiary. “As government, we are confident we will host a successful AFCON.” The next three months are likely to be particularly crucial in making that promise a reality.

items.title: ICE agent shoots and wounds man in Texas as locals demand answers
items.description: Protesters have gathered in Austin, Texas where local officials said a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent shot and wounded a man in the Texas capital. Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a 28-year-old Venezuelan national, was shot in the torso and taken to the hospital, his lawyer has told US media. Local officials are seeking answers from federal authorities and could not say whether he was a target of ICE. The mayor and police have demanded an independent probe, with this shooting coming months after a man in Houston, Texas was shot dead by an ICE officer. The BBC has contacted ICE and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). Attorney Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch told CBS that Garces Perez called his wife while “yelling in pain” in hospital. She told National Public Radio he was in ICE custody. The shooting on Sunday in Austin occurred just before 1300 local time, although details remain scarce. Dozens of protesters, some waving the flags of Mexico and Guatemala, have since gathered at the scene carrying signs demanding that ICE leave Austin. Local television outlets showed the demonstrators gathering across the street from ​a blue Toyota Corolla that ⁠sustained damage to the passenger-side door, as ICE agents stood nearby, Reuters news agency reported. Mayor Kirk Watson, a Democrat, said that Austinites have a right to know what happened and “a right to feel safe in their city” during a media briefing on Sunday. “They should know the truth” he said, adding that he is pleased that the city will also be involved in the investigation. He added that ICE operations have surged in Austin in recent weeks. ICE has faced intense scrutiny after a number of deadly shootings, including the death of Houston resident Lorenzo Salgado Araujo. Salgado Araujo had not been a target of an ICE investigation, but was shot during an ICE traffic stop, according to DHS . Texas Congressman Greg Casar, a Democrat, has demanded a full and immediate independent investigation and the release of body camera footage. He also demanded “accountability for any ICE officer who broke the law”. The Austin Police Department confirmed to a local CBS News affiliate that the victim was injured and was transported to hospital. No Austin police officer was involved in the shooting. The Trump administration has ramped up immigration enforcement efforts and arrests during Trump’s second term, which sparked unrest across several US cities. The administration has defended its policies and the agency’s controversial tactics as necessary for public safety and to carry out Trump’s mass deportations mandate. But rights activists say that the administration has violated free speech and due process rights and Democrats have demanded reforms at the agency, including requiring immigration enforcement agents to wear body cameras and barring them from concealing their faces during operations. Earlier this month the US Department of Justice charged an ICE agent with lying about the non-fatal shooting of a Venezuelan migrant in Minnesota – a rare instance in which the current justice department accused a federal agent of breaking the law on the job. Earlier this week, Florida lawmaker Maria Elvira Salazar, a Republican who has been spoken out against the immigration crackdown, released an advert critcising the targeting and detaining of individuals who have no criminal record. Salazar appeared on the CBS programme Face the Nation on Sunday and said that she has since spoken to the president, and believes he will keep the country on the right track. “He gets it more than anybody,” she said.

items.title: Naqvi due in Iran for talks as Hormuz terms conveyed
items.description: TEHRAN: With Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi due in Iran for talks on Sunday, Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has said that terms for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz have been clearly conveyed to the United States through mediators. “Our messages and the explanation of our conditions have been clearly conveyed to the other party through mediators,” said Iran’s chi­ef negotiator in talks to end the war. “As long as the conditions are not met… and the US commitments are not honoured, it will be impossible to return to the situation from before the negotiations and to an open strait,” he added. In a post on X, Mr Ghalibaf wrote, “It’s Schrödinger: the em­­pire is in the SOH [Strait of Hor­muz] cabinet with falling plates, projecting hegemony but fully exposed, trying to suffocate Iran without blowback (impossible).” “This endgame cannot be modelled. It will be opened, and Iran’s hand is already on the lever,” he said, sharing a recent note by JPMorgan wherein analysts said they “simply don’t know how to model the endgame” to the oil market crisis. Also, Mohsen Rezaei, the head of supreme national security council, earlier said Iran had conveyed its conditions to the US via mediator Qatar. “Our conditions are an end to the war on all fronts, the release of our frozen funds and an end to the naval blockade,” he said, in an interview with Al Jazeera. He warned that the US would face an Iran that was better prepared than at the start of the war. The Iranian security chief said Iran had increased the speed of its hypersonic missiles from Mach-6 to Mach-10, improved air defences and developed electronic warfare systems. “Therefore should war break out again, US ships, unless they withdraw from the Indian Ocean, will be subject to attack.” Also, Iran’s Khatam al-Anbiya central military command warned that if the US made a mistake in dealing with Iran, all of its bases and interests in the region would become the target of continuous, effective and painful attacks, without any limit or restraint. Published in Dawn, September 21st, 2026

items.title: Trump mulls next moves on Iran amid ominous warnings
items.description: • State Dept warns Americans to brace for ‘unforeseen escalation’ across the Middle East • Trump abruptly leaves Camp David; tells Fox News ‘if and when I blow entire nation up is my question’; claims Houthis agreed not to fight US • Iran threatens ‘sustained retaliation’; says Washington allies will be considered party to conflict • PM Shehbaz to highlight mediatory role at UNGA, says envoy WASHINGTON: The United States issued fresh security warnings for Americans in the Middle East on Sunday, cautioning that the security environment remained volatile and could face an “unforeseen escalation” as President Donald Trump considers his next steps in the war with Iran. Trump cut short a weekend at Camp David, returning unannounced to the White House on Saturday evening as the White House offered no explanation for the abrupt change of plan, which comes just days before he is due in New York for the UN General Assembly. The warnings, circulated through US diplomatic missions in the region, urged Americans currently in the Middle East to exercise heightened vigilance and prepare for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions. Americans outside the region were advised to “seriously reconsider travel to and through the region”. “Due to tensions in the Middle East, the security environment remains complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation,” the State Department said in its alerts. “Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports. This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly.” Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also cut short his US visit and returned to Israel, adding to the uncertainty surrounding the region. Trump’s next move Trump has indicated that he faces a major decision over whether to intensify the conflict. The US president told Fox News that he is in “deciding mode” on Iran and “big things will be happening in the not-so-distant future”. According to network’s Trey Yingst, the president outlined the options as “wiping Iran out, letting them rot economically, or making a deal”. Trump reportedly added, “My question is, if and when do I blow the entire nation up? They [Iranians] better behave.” When asked about meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who will be attending the UN General Assembly in New York this week, Trump said he would ‘probably be open’ to it. In an interview with Axios earlier this week, Trump said: “I have a big decision coming up. Do I want to go in and annihilate them, or do I not? It’s a big decision. Anything could happen with me.” On the other hand, Trump reiterated that Houthis agreed not to attack the United States, Fox News reported. He also claimed a week ago the Houthis were holding back from attacking US forces in the region. “The Houthis called us and they don’t want to fight with us,” Trump said during a visit to Ireland on Sept 12. “They don’t want us to go after them.” Sustained retaliation Meanwhile, Iran warned on Sunday against any big new attack by the US and its allies, saying it had information such a move was being prepared, adding to the anxiety in a region already on edge. Iran’s military central command said on state media that any new attack would trigger sustained retaliation against US bases and interests and that Washington’s regional allies would be considered parties to the conflict. It did not elaborate on the information it said it had about a coming US attack. Mediatory role Meanwhile, briefing journalists ahead of the 81st UN General Assembly session , Pakistan’s Ambassador to the UN Asim Iftikhar Ahmad said that Islamabad will stress its mediatory role amid the widening Middle East crisis during the high-level week of the UN General Assembly. He said that PM Shehbaz Sharif’s address on the 25th would present Pakistan’s perspective on the evolving regional and international security environment and emphasising dialogue, diplomacy, restraint and the peaceful resolution of disputes. Pakistan, the ambassador said, would also use the high-level week to underline its constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability and its resolve to work with UN member states to uphold the UN Charter, strengthen multilateralism, prevent conflict and advance international cooperation. Published in Dawn, September 21st, 2026

items.title: Govt vows not to allow ‘violent groups’ to reach capital
items.description: • Tarar says IHC ruling bars disruption of public movement, road closures • Protests may cost economy Rs120bn per day, Aurangzeb warns ISLAMABAD: Information Min­ister Attaullah Tarar on Sunday said the government would not allow any violent group to reach Islamabad or block roads, as ministers warned of the legal, economic and law-and-order consequences of upcoming protests by Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf and Jamaat-i-Islami. Speaking to the media, Mr Tarar said the planned protests had both legal and administrative aspects, stressing that the Islamabad High Court (IHC) had clearly ruled against road closures and disruption to public movement. He said it was now the responsibility of the administration to ens­ure that no such disruption took place. “No violent group will be all­owed to reach Islamabad,” he said. “The administration, police, interior minister and entire government are absolutely clear” on the matter, he said, adding that protesters intending to cause disruption would not be allowed to reach the capital and roads would remain open. Mr Tarar said the government remained in contact with JI at different levels, including its top leadership. He described the party’s leaders as peaceful and flexible but stressed that the law applied equally to everyone and roads could not be blocked. The remarks come as PTI prepares for a nationwide protest and march towards Islamabad on Sept 27 to press for the release of its incarcerated founder Imran Khan, while JI has launched a protest campaign against the petroleum levy and plans to head towards the federal capital. Rs120bn daily loss feared Separately, Finance Minister Muha­mmad Aurangzeb warned that strikes, sit-ins, long marches and road closures could inflict an estimated Rs120 billion loss on the economy every day at a time when it was moving from stability towards growth. In a recorded message, Mr Aurangzeb said economic indicators had been moving in a positive direction after difficult decisions and considerable effort. “Suspension of economic activities due to strikes, sit-ins, long marches and closure of roads could be a self-inflicted loss,” he said, adding that the burden would ultimately be borne by ordinary people, small traders and shopkeepers. Citing estimates prepared jointly by the Planning Commission and Ministry of Finance, he said the services sector — including financial services, communication, retail, transportation, wholesale and hospitality — could suffer the largest daily loss of around Rs86bn. The industrial sector could lose around Rs25bn, including losses in construction, finished goods, raw materials and supply chains, while agriculture could suffer losses of Rs9bn. An additional revenue loss of about Rs17bn a day was also expected in case of disruption to economic activity. Mr Aurangzeb said businesses and exporters were already facing pressures from disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, higher freight and insurance costs, while the country was also confronting a fresh wave of terrorism. He warned that fresh political disruption could undermine the government’s export-led growth plans. The export target for the current fiscal year stood at $35.9bn, with growth of six per cent expected, he said. “We have been on trajectory for the first two months,” he said, recalling that the economy had taken around one and a half months to recover from losses caused by a strike in December 2025. He also pointed to the possible impact on IT exports, saying they stood at $811 million during July and August, averaging around $13m a day. He said internet connectivity disruptions during previous episodes of civil disobedience had affected IT exports by as much as 80pc. The finance minister said it was his responsibility to present the facts, figures and possible downside of what he described as “self-inflicted pain” and called for dialogue to resolve outstanding and political issues. Concern over PTI remarks Meanwhile, Minister for Parli­amentary Affairs Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said recent statements by PTI leaders regarding their planned march towards Islamabad had raised concerns about possible violence. Speaking to a private television channel, he referred to a reported statement by a senior PTI leader that the protesters were coming to make Islamabad “Somnath”. Mr Chaudhry described the remark as a threat and said the government had a responsibility to protect the federal capital, maintain peace and ensure that normal life was not disrupted. “Islamabad is the city of all Pakistanis, and no one will be allowed to deteriorate its law-and-order situation,” he said. Asked about JI’s protests, Mr Chaudhry said the party had no history of protests turning violent or undermining law and order. He said the government had held several rounds of talks with JI over the issue and expressed hope that the matter would be resolved through dialogue. With additional input from APP Published in Dawn, September 21st, 2026

items.title: Ed Sheeran admits ‘mistakes’ at first show since Macklemore controversy
items.description: Ed Sheeran has apologised to fans for making “mistakes” as he opened his first show since Macklemore was dropped from his tour for making pro-Palestinian remarks on stage. The singer began his concert in Philadelphia by addressing the controversy that has since engulfed the tour and prompted all of his support acts to quit. “I never wanted to be an activist musician, but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about free speech and the most complex political issue on the planet,” Sheeran said. He described the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attacks as “horrific” and called the situation in Gaza “unjustifiable”. The singer has said the decision to drop Macklemore was made by his promoters, not him. The row has seen ticket prices drop and sales decline for the remaining US leg of his Loop Tour. Sheeran told the crowd that while he was used to facing criticism for his music, “this week, the criticism was about something much more important, and I’ve had to take and make difficult decisions – and I am making mistakes – and I’m so, so sorry”. He said he wanted to “address the question of where I stand in the situation in Israel and Palestine, and whether my doing this concert here tonight implies where I stand”. “I have tried in my career not to be a political commentator of any kind, because I want my music and shows to be about unity, not division”, he continued. “But this is a humanitarian issue, and I cannot hide how I feel about it anymore.” Sheeran said what happened in Israel on 7 October was “horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain”, and what was happening in Gaza was “catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate”. “My heart has been broken by the scale of devastation and loss of civilian lives, of children’s lives, and this systemic injustice we’re seeing unfold in the West Bank cannot be overlooked.” He said he was working out how to contribute in a way that would help “victims of these terrible times – and listening and learning, because I do not know enough”. The British singer became emotional as he told the crowd his concert was “still a place where everyone is welcome, and everyone here can stand beside people that have opposing views”. He said that he had not known “whether this tour would be carrying on” and “whether I even wanted to be an artist at all”, but that he had returned to the stage because he was committed to his fans. Sheeran also said he was “deeply worried” about venues “pre-approve” content or performers, a point that drew applause from the audience. His remaining tour dates are scheduled with shows set throughout North and South America. While the mega-star’s previous tour was among the highest-grossing of all time, some ticket prices for this show dropped to $32 (£24). Some fans reported being able to get ticket refunds, though Ticketmaster and concert promoter Messina Touring Group did not confirm they were being reimbursed. Some protesters waved flags outside the venue, but the concert proceeded largely unfettered. A protester who gave his name as Cooper said he had come out “to support the struggle for” the Palestinian people. “We need more people like Macklemore and other artists who have a voice, who have a public platform, to be able to speak on behalf of the Palestinian people and their struggle for liberation, especially in the United States,” he said. Of the handful of ticket-holders who stopped to talk to the BBC prior to the show, there was a sentiment of determination to enjoy an evening of music while at the same time supporting freedom of speech. Reacting to Sheeran’s remarks as they later left the venue, one fan said he had “covered both sides nicely, and I think everyone leaves happy”, while another called his speech “very sincere, and I think that’s what the people wanted to hear was sincerity”. The controversy began in early September, when Macklemore performed a song dedicated to pro-Palestinian protesters and referred to the death toll in Gaza as a genocide, a claim Israel rejects. The rapper also said criticism of Israel was not intended as criticism of “my Jewish brothers and sisters”. Messina Touring Group said Macklemore was dropped because some venues – such as Gillette Stadium in Boston, Massachusetts – would refuse to let the concerts take place if he performed. Billionaire Robert Kraft who owns Gillette Stadium and the American football team the New England Patriots, confirmed he had banned Macklemore from performing during the British singer’s forthcoming shows. Kraft, who is Jewish, accused the US rapper of hate speech and said he was “only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas”. Meanwhile, support acts including Irish singer-songwriter Aaron Rowe and Danish musician Lukas Graham and his backing band Beoga quit the tour in solidarity with Macklemore. The artists argued his removal represented a chilling effect on free speech.

items.title: Sénégal: le plus beau but de Sadio Mané, sans ballon!
items.description: Un goleador de 34 ans, qui a fait trembler les filets des gardiens de grands championnats et de prestigieuses compétitions comme la Coupe d’Afrique des Nations, qu’il a remportée en 2025 avec les Lions de la Teranga, ou de la Champions League ou encore de la Coupe du monde. Ainsi se définit Sadio Mané. Mais son plus beau but, l’enfant de Bambali ne l’a pas marqué sur un terrain de football, mais dans son village natal en Casamance, où il vient de mettre en route, avec des partenaires à lui, un immense projet de transformation agro-industriel. En posant la première pierre de ce site de transformation de la mangue et qui devrait, à terme, coûter 11,7 milliards de francs CFA, le coéquipier de Cristiano Ronaldo, signe un acte indélébile pour la postérité. Et ce n’est pas avec un ballon de football! Celui qui a fait les beaux jours des célèbres Reds de Liverpool en Premier League anglaise et des «Roten» ou Rouges du Bayern de Munich en Bundesliga allemande, avant de promener désormais ses crampons sur les pelouses saoudiennes avec Al-Nassr FC, a réellement fait œuvre utile pour le développement et la souveraineté de son pays et le mieux-être de ses compatriotes. Sadio Mané vient de donner la preuve, en présence de personnalités politiques, et pas des moindres, que ce n’est pas seulement en tant que président de la république, ou patron de l’Assemblée nationale, ou encore ministre du gouvernement, etc., que l’on peut tracer les sillons d’un avenir radieux pour la jeunesse d’une région, la Casamance et d’un pays, le Sénégal. Lorsqu’il sera érigé et fonctionnel, c’est la transformation de 8500 tonnes de fruits que SM10 Agro sera en mesure de réaliser, selon les projections, mais ce sera, surtout, la création de plus de 1000 emplois directs qui sera concrétisée au profit d’une jeunesse sénégalaise jusqu’ici très attirée par le vent de l’aventure et persuadée que l’eldorado se trouve derrière la Méditerranée. Ainsi donc, ce sont des milliers de vie qui seront sauvées, elles qui ont longtemps été avalées par les océans, ou fauchées pas les balles de gardes-côtes à la gâchette facile, au pied de la citadelle désormais imprenable de l’Europe. A n’en point douter, cette révolution industrielle, tout en ouvrant la voie financièrement juteuse de l’exportation aux mangues casamançaises, leur évitera également de pourrir, par tonnes, dans les vergers, par manque de débouchés sur le marché international. SM10 Agro, offrira donc une source importante de revenu à des générations de producteurs de mangues sénégalais. Certes des difficultés qui pourraient avoir pour noms mauvaise gestion, enclavement de la Casamance, et détournement de la vision noble par des politiciens aux intérêts égoïstes et très personnels, ne sont pas à écarter. Mais elles ne seront pas non plus incontournables, si le projet demeure dans la droite ligne que lui a tracée son fondateur. En tout cas, par le biais de cet investissement, Sadio Mané qui ne se contente plus de donner du poisson aux siens, mais met entre leurs mains l'outil à pêcher le poisson, montre une fois de plus le secours important de la diaspora à leurs parents restés en Afrique. Mais, ils invite aussi, ces diasporas à passer du patrimoine personnel et familial à la création de richesse collective. Question: pourquoi, à l’instar de nombre de footballeurs professionnels africains fortunés, l’international sénégalais n’a-t-il pas plutôt investi dans un centre de formation de football? D’autres l’ont déjà fait et le feront! «Nous voulons contribuer à créer de l’emploi et à développer l’agriculture», a dit Sadio Mané. Mais pas que! «L’ambition est aussi de montrer qu’un jeune de Casamance peut construire son avenir sur sa propre terre sans être obligé de partir ailleurs pour chercher les possibilités qui lui manquent ici». Ainsi a parlé le virtuose du ballon rond, convaincu que SM10 Agro peut devenir une solide digue contre l’immigration massive d’une jeunesse sénégalaise pour qui, comme pour d’autres jeunesses de pays africains, la Méditerranée s’est transformée en un géant cimetière à ciel ouvert! Par Wakat Séra L’article Sénégal: le plus beau but de Sadio Mané, sans ballon! est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: We are ready for the turbulence – NPA boss on Ghana’s fuel crisis
items.description: The CEO of the National Petroleum Authority (NPA), Godwin Edudzi Tamakloe, says the Authority is prepared to address turbulence in Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector as international market pressures continue to drive up fuel prices. His comments come at a time when Ghana’s fuel market is facing renewed pressure from higher international prices for crude and refined petroleum products. The NPA increased the price floor for petrol to GH¢16 per litre and diesel to GH¢16.77 per litre from September 16. Some Oil Marketing Companies have since raised pump prices, with Star Oil pricing petrol at GH¢16.77 and diesel at GH¢17.77 per litre. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday, Mr Tamakloe said his preparation for the job has always included the possibility of major disruptions in the petroleum market. He said Ghana is largely dependent on imports for refined petroleum products, leaving the sector exposed to external shocks. “Having to be the Chief Executive Officer of the downstream, I appreciated the fact that we are primarily import-dependent when it comes to refined petroleum products.” He said this exposure means the industry can face turbulence whenever external conditions change. “So, I’ve always been, you know, let me say, ready for the potential for turbulence.” Mr Tamakloe said managing such pressures has therefore been part of his orientation since taking charge of the sector. “It’s been part of the orientation that I’ve had personally, that you are going to, as it were, lead or take charge of an industry that is largely subject to, or, you know, will face turbulence at any time that exogenous or external factors change.” He said effective leadership requires a response whether conditions are favourable or difficult. “What I believe is that leadership in this particular instance, there are issues, and we believe that in good or bad times, you need to have a leadership response to both sides.” The NPA boss said the Authority has been dealing with the current turbulence since February. “And so, I would say that we are kind of ready, and from February till now, we’ve been trying to, as it were, manage the turbulence, manage the storm.” He acknowledged the pressure facing the sector but said the response so far had been positive. “And the management so far has not been bad at all.”

items.title: Lady I wanted serious relationship with said she’s not ready – Rema
items.description: Nigerian singer Divine Ikubor, popularly known as Rema, has revealed that he recently experienced heartbreak after a woman rejected his proposal for a long-term relationship. Speaking during a livestream with streamer Okiki on Friday night, Rema disclosed that he approached a lady for a “serious relationship,” but she turned him down because she was not ready to commit to one man. Rema emphasised that the lady told him she still wanted to explore life as a single woman and did not want to be taken “off the streets” yet. The 26-year-old musician revealed that the heartbreak inspired his song, ‘Oh No.’ “The song was inspired by a lady I wanted a serious relationship with, but she said she still wants to be on the streets,” he said. Rema also shared that he is taking time to re-evaluate his life because “everything moved so fast” after he became famous at 17.

items.title: JCI Agoè-Nyivé Pioneer : Bilan à mi-parcours du mandat 2026 et élection d’un nouveau bureau à la COLOC
items.description: Lomé, 20 sept. (ATOP) – La Jeune chambre internationale (JCI) Agoè-Nyivé Pioneer a fait, le samedi 19 septembre à Lomé, le bilan à mi-parcours de sa Convention locale (COLOC) 2026, autour du thème « Impacter efficacement », couplée de l’élection d’un nouveau bureau. Les travaux ont été lancés par le représentant du préfet d’Agoè-Nyivé M. Kodjoukabalo Pewili. La rencontre a pour objectif de faire le bilan des actions menées au cours de la première partie du mandat, d’évaluer les résultats obtenus et de définir les orientations pour la suite de l’exercice. Au-delà de l’aspect institutionnel, le mandat 2026 a été placé sous le signe de l’impact communautaire. Dans cette dynamique, deux projets communautaires ont été inscrits au plan d’action notamment la sensibilisation à la trisomie 21, marquée par l’organisation d’un gala de charité et le projet « Assiménéko », réalisé avec la commune Agoè-Nyivé 1, au niveau du marché d’Agoè-Assiyé. Le mandat a également été marqué par l’organisation d’une méga-masterclass destinée aux entrepreneurs. Les participants ont suivi la présentation des rapports des différentes instances de la JCI Agoè-Nyivé Pioneer. Ils ont apprécié le niveau de réalisation des activités programmées, les acquis enregistrés ainsi que les difficultés rencontrées. Les membres ont procédé à l’élection des futurs dirigeants de la JCI Agoè-Nyivé Pioneer, conformément au principe de renouvellement du leadership au sein de l’organisation. C’est Mme Grace Akouvi Kouawu qui prendra désormais les rênes de l’organisation pour un mandat d’un an non renouvelable. Elle préside un bureau de quatre membres. Une communication sur le rôle du leadership entrepreneurial dans le développement local a été également présentée. Les échanges ont mis l’accent sur la nécessité pour les jeunes leaders de contribuer à la création de valeur, à la promotion de l’entrepreneuriat et à la recherche de solutions aux défis locaux. M. Kodjoukabalo Pewili, a souligné que le thème constitue à la fois un défi et une interpellation pour les jeunes membres de l’organisation. Il traduit, selon lui, la volonté d’aller au-delà des discours pour privilégier des actions concrètes, mesurables et durables au bénéfice des communautés. ATOP/AO/SED

items.title: Législatives 2026 : Nabil Benabdallah critique un gouvernement de "conflits d'intérêts" et appelle au vote sanction
items.description: Lors d'un meeting électoral populaire tenu à Tanger ce dimanche soir, Mohamed Nabil Benabdallah, secrétaire général du Parti du Progrès et du Socialisme (PPS), a lancé un appel direct aux habitants de la ville du Nord et à l'ensemble des Marocains pour un vote sanction massif, afin de barrer la route au retour des partis de l'exécutif, qu'il a qualifié de « gouvernement des conflits d'intérêts ». Attaquant le gouvernement d'Aziz Akhannouch, Benabdallah a déclaré que l'histoire du Maroc « n'a jamais connu un gouvernement incarnant à ce point les conflits d'intérêts, la corruption et la connivence, comme nous l'avons vu avec cette équipe ». Le secrétaire général du parti du « Livre » a souligné que « les spéculateurs (frakchia) sont les maîtres de ce gouvernement que nous avons combattu pendant des années et qui a provoqué la détérioration du pouvoir d'achat des citoyens, lesquels souffrent de la cherté de la vie dans tout le pays ». Il a estimé que l'exécutif « n'a pas été à la hauteur ; il a plutôt encouragé et fait preuve de connivence avec un ensemble de lobbies et de complexes d'intérêts économiques ». Benabdallah a précisé : « Dans tous les quartiers de Tanger, comme dans l'ensemble des provinces, préfectures, villes et villages, personne ne dit du bien de ce gouvernement ni ne le défend », appelant à traduire cette grande colère en acte concret dans les urnes. Il a ajouté : « Il ne faut pas qu'aujourd'hui tout le monde soit d'accord pour dire que nous sommes face à un gouvernement qui a essuyé un échec cuisant, et que demain nous soyons surpris par les résultats. Pourquoi ? Parce que les gens n'auront pas été voter », estimant que le défi majeur pour les Marocains au cours des deux prochains jours réside dans un « vote utile et sanction ». Benabdallah a accusé plusieurs candidats en lice dans une ville comme Tanger de recourir aux « mêmes méthodes, en utilisant l'argent et en employant des milliers de personnes dans leurs campagnes électorales », s'interrogeant : « Nous ne savons pas d'où ils tirent ces fonds. Ils les tirent de la corruption. Et ils veulent accéder de nouveau aux institutions élues pour nous refaire un gouvernement similaire, afin qu'ils soient couverts à nouveau et cela leur permette de poursuivre leurs pratiques et l'exploitation des deniers publics. » L'intervenant a réservé une critique particulièrement vive à Aziz Akhannouch, chef du gouvernement, en rappelant le dossier des carburants et les ententes illicites constatées : « Certaines sociétés de carburants se sont entendues entre elles, parmi elles, une société présidée par le chef du gouvernement, accumulant des milliards de bénéfices illicites, ce qu'a confirmé le Conseil de la concurrence. » Benabdallah a reconnu que les prix du pétrole avaient en effet enregistré une hausse au niveau international, « mais les gouvernements de nombreux pays ont pris leurs responsabilités, soutenu les prix et réduit la TVA ainsi que la taxe intérieure de consommation (TIC), tandis que notre gouvernement n'a rien fait de tout cela ». Le secrétaire général du PPS a également critiqué les affrontements électoraux entre les partis de la coalition gouvernementale, l'instrumentalisation du dossier des « spéculateurs » et l'échange d'accusations à ce sujet dans le cadre d'une « rivalité électorale et politicienne misérable, alors qu'ils appartiennent au même gouvernement ». À cet égard, le dirigeant politique a affirmé que « le gouvernement, avec l'ensemble de ses composantes, et à sa tête le parti du chef du gouvernement, porte la responsabilité de ce qui se passe ». Mohamed Nabil Benabdallah s'est dit fier que son parti ait été à l'origine de la révélation de ce dossier et d'autres affaires attestant de l'implication du gouvernement dans les conflits d'intérêts et la corruption. Il a enfin démenti que le gouvernement ait généralisé la couverture médicale à l'ensemble des Marocains, pointant du doigt des chiffres officiels qui font état de 11 millions de Marocains toujours privés de couverture santé. The post Législatives 2026 : Nabil Benabdallah critique un gouvernement de "conflits d'intérêts" et appelle au vote sanction appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: I’ll never discuss my finances with man, even if he’s my husband – Nancy Isime
items.description: Nollywood actor and media personality Nancy Isime has said she would never discuss her finances with a man she is in a relationship with. Speaking in an episode of the Thanks for Coming podcast, Isime emphasised that she would not disclose her earnings even to her husband. She explained that she does not see any need for that, stressing that she also does not expect her partner to discuss his finances with her. “I will never discuss three things: my money, my money, my money. I would never discuss how much I have in my account or how much I earn with my man. For what? He shouldn’t discuss his either with me,” she said. She also said that she would never check her man’s phone, adding that she does not care that much. Isime advised ladies who check their partners’ phones to refrain from doing so and stop putting so much pressure on themselves.

items.title: Bassar : Formation des acteurs sur la gestion de la chefferie coutumière
items.description: Bassar, 20 sept. (ATOP) – Le ministère de l’Administration territorial a initiée une rencontre de renforcement de capacités des acteurs pour une gestion non conflictuelle de la chefferie traditionnelle le vendredi 18 septembre à Bassar. L’atelier a réuni les préfets, les secrétaires généraux, les maires, les garants des us et coutumes de Mô, Dankpen et de Bassar. L’objectif est d’outiller les acteurs concernés sur le cadre légal de la chefferie coutumière et s ur la bonne gestion de la chefferie coutumière. Il s’agit aussi de prévenir les situations conflictuelles, de consolider le dialogue entre les différents acteurs, de promouvoir la responsabilité dans l’exercice des fonctions coutumières et de contribuer à prévenir les incompréhensions susceptibles de fragiliser la cohésion sociale au sein des communautés. Les participants ont suivi une formation sur les notions et connaissances des textes et principes qui régissent la chefferie traditionnelle. Trois communications ont été dispensées aux participants à savoir le cadre juridique et institutionnel de la chefferie traditionnelle, les rôles et responsabilités des acteurs, ainsi que les mécanismes favorisant une gestion harmonieuse des questions coutumières. Les participants ont été également situés sur les organes de désignation des chefs traditionnels et leur fonctionnement, ainsi que les différentes étapes d’une procédure de reconnaissance d’un candidat-chef. Le préfet de Bassar Lt-col Asiah Hodabalo a invité tous les acteurs impliqués à relayer les enseignements reçus aux autres acteurs concernés et à les mettre en application. « La formation qui nous rassemble aujourd’hui est un instrument majeur de cette politique de prévention et de règlement pacifique des différends coutumiers » a-t-il réitéré. « La gestion de la chefferie traditionnelle pose de nos jours des inquiétudes, elle souffre de récurrentes contestations qui vont même aux contentieux de successions, des rivalités entre princes et princesses » a fait savoir le directeur de la Chefferie traditionnelle, Massimlawé Wazabalo. Il a invité les participants à s’approprier des bonnes pratiques afin d’améliorer sensiblement la gestion de la chefferie traditionnelle et de prévenir les conflits. La prochaine étape de cette formation est prévue à Sokodé le 21 septembre, et Atakpamé, Kpalimé, Tsévié et Adétikopé du 22 au 26 septembre prochain. ATOP/LK/AR/KYA

items.title: Face-à-face à Kaya : Le ministre de la Défense dresse le bilan de la reconquête militaire sous le MPSR2
items.description: En direct depuis Kaya, siège de la première région militaire, le ministre d'État, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, le général de division Célestin Simporé, s'est prêté pendant près de deux heures aux questions des journalistes et des auditeurs dans l'émission « Antenne directe » de Radio Burkina. Revenant sur les actions menées sous le MPSR2 autour de la transformation de la défense nationale et de la souveraineté militaire, le chef du département de la Défense a dressé un bilan marqué par la réinstallation des populations et le contrôle de plus de 74 % du territoire national. C'est à Kaya, au sein de la première région militaire, que le général de division Célestin Simporé, ministre d'État, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, est intervenu sur les antennes de la radio nationale. Durant près de deux heures d'entretien interactif avec des journalistes et des auditeurs, le ministre a exposé les acquis, les défis et les perspectives de son département sous le MPSR2. Axée sur le thème de la transformation de la défense nationale, de la reconquête du territoire et de la souveraineté militaire, cette intervention a permis de souligner les avancées enregistrées dans la lutte contre le terrorisme, concrétisées notamment par la réinstallation progressive des populations dans plusieurs localités. Du manque d'équipements initial au contrôle de plus de 74 % du territoire Revenant sur les débuts de la crise sécuritaire, le général Célestin Simporé a rappelé que le pays avait dû recourir à l’emprunt d'armes auprès de certains pays pour faire face à la menace terroriste. Depuis cette période où le contrôle n'était que d'environ 40 %, la situation sur le terrain a évolué : plus de 74 % du territoire burkinabè est désormais sous contrôle. Apportant une précision sur la notion de reconquête, le ministre a expliqué qu'il s'agit de zones stabilisées et sécurisées afin de permettre un retour effectif et durable de la vie quotidienne. Enjeux géopolitiques et synergie au sein de l'AES Abordant les ressorts du conflit, le ministre d'État a soutenu que la guerre imposée au Burkina Faso découle d'une opposition géopolitique et d'intérêts impérialistes visant l'exploitation des ressources du pays, qualifiant la menace terroriste de simple façade. Dans ce contexte, le général Simporé a salué la bonne coopération entre les armées membres de l'Alliance des États du Sahel (AES), avant de réaffirmer sa conviction que le combat mené par le pays connaîtra une issue victorieuse. L’article Face-à-face à Kaya : Le ministre de la Défense dresse le bilan de la reconquête militaire sous le MPSR2 est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Wizkid, Wande Coal advised me on how to leave school for music – Davido
items.description: Famous singer David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, has revealed that he consulted his colleagues, Wizkid and Wande Coal, in the early stages of his career on how to combine music with schooling. Speaking in the Afrobeats Documentary, Davido revealed that the duo told him the only way he could leave school and focus on music was to achieve stardom. The singer said he knew his father would not allow him to abandon his education for music, but after his song, ‘Dami Duro’, became a hit, he could no longer continue schooling. “I asked Wizkid and Wande Coal how they left school to do music. “They told me the only way was to blow up. I knew my dad wouldn’t allow me, but when ‘Dami Duro’ blew up, I couldn’t continue,” he said. Davido later returned to school, juggling his studies with music after reaching an agreement with his father to go back to school in exchange for access to a recording studio and his father’s express permission to pursue his musical career. He graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Music from Babcock University in 2015.

items.title: Tchamba/ Religion : El Hadj Oniankitan Moukaïla reconnu officiellement, Imam principal de Kaboli
items.description: Tchamba, 20 sept. (ATOP) – Désigné par la communauté musulmane, El Hadj Oniankitan Moukaïla a été intronisé et reconnu officiellement, le samedi 19 septembre, imam principal de Kaboli, à l’est de Tchamba, dans la commune Tchamba 3. La cérémonie a été présidée par le préfet de Tchamba, Issaka Laguebande en présence du sénateur Drama Dramani. Cette investiture vise à renforcer l’enseignement religieux et la cohésion sociale. Elle a été marquée par la prière de circonstance, la lecture du Saint Coran, le rituel d’intronisation (pose du turban et du vêtement d’imam) et la remise du bâton de commandement par le président de l’Union Musulmane Togo (UMT), section Tchaoudjo, Katakpaou Sagnadou. L’autre temps fort a été la remise de l’attestation de reconnaissance par le préfet Issaka. L’impétrant a bénéficié des conseils des dignitaires musulmans de la région et du milieu, ainsi que des prières pour la réussite de sa mission. M. Katakpaou remettant le bâton de commandement à El Hadj Oniankitan Le président de l’UMT, section Tchaoudjo a requis du récipiendaire, le travail bien fait pour l’union des musulmans de Kaboli, la collaboration avec les autorités locales et le soutien aux personnes vulnérables. Il a exhorté le nouvel imam à promouvoir la cohésion sociale, le vivre ensemble et la cohabitation avec toutes les autres confessions religieuses dans la localité. M. Katakpaou a demandé à tous ses coreligionnaires et tous les croyants collectivement ou individuellement, d’invoquer Allah afin qu’il débarrasse le Togo des ennemis de la paix pour son développement. Le préfet a appelé tous les musulmans à soutenir leur imam principal et à l’accompagner pour le développement de la communauté. Il a invité le nouvel imam à toujours demander la clémence d’Allah pour mener à bien sa mission. Le nouvel imam El Hadj Oniankitan a rendu grâce à Allah qui a permis sa désignation. Il a promis de guider, fidèlement, la communauté dans la voie islamique, de préserver les valeurs religieuses et de veiller au respect des traditions. El Hadj Oniankitan a convié les fidèles à cultiver, en tout temps, la tolérance et le dialogue. Le nouveau guide spirituel a prié pour la consolidation de la paix dans le pays et pour les dirigeants. Agé de 69 ans, El Hadj Oniankitan Moukaïla succède à l’imam Ogbone Abdoul-Karimou, décédé le 27 mai 2022 à Kaboli. ATOP/SA/MEK/AR
