items.title: Senegal job an ‘absolute dream’ for new boss Vieira
items.description: Patrick Vieira says it is “an honour” to become Senegal head coach, with the decision to take the job “one from the heart”. The 50-year-old was born in a West African nation but later represented France, winning the 1998 World Cup and the 2000 European Championship with Les Bleus. The former Arsenal midfielder spoke of his “immense pride” to begin his first international job, following stints with New York City, Nice, Crystal Palace, Strasbourg and Genoa, at his unveiling by the Teranga Lions on Friday. “Being head coach of the Senegal national team is an absolute dream,” he told a news conference in Dakar. “I was born here, my parents were born here, and it really is a homecoming. “From the very first meetings I had with the [Senegal football federation] president, I accepted this challenge straight away, because there was also an exceptional generation of players. “I realise the expectations of the people – all 20 million Senegalese. And I know that with the experience I have, with the determination I have, I’ll be able to see this project through.” Taking over after the dismissal of Pape Thiaw, Vieira inherits a Senegal side which exited the 2026 World Cup in dramatic fashion in the last 32, throwing away a 2-0 lead after 85 minutes against Belgium before losing 3-2 following extra time. Before that the Teranga Lions claimed the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) title with a 1-0 extra-time win over Morocco in January. However, the ultimate destination of the trophy will be decided by the Court of Arbitration for Sport after a walk-off by some Senegal players and staff protesting against a penalty decision in the final resulted in the trophy being handed to the North African hosts instead in March. “Today, Senegal is among the major nations in world football,” Vieira said. “Senegal’s objectives aren’t what they were 10 or 15 years ago. On the back of its recent results, Senegal has moved forward, has reached new levels. “The demand for results has also stepped up. We need to lay solid foundations.” Vieira plans to build a side with “a very precise structure” which can play with “intensity and aggression”. “What matters to me isn’t starting again from scratch,” he added. “It’s about respecting what the federation has put in place over the last few years and building the next stage, opening a new chapter. “A new chapter meaning my job isn’t to tear everything down, it isn’t to throw everything out of the window. “It’s about keeping this team’s strength: its identity, its unity, its ability to suffer together. “To make this project work, I’ll need the whole nation united. I’ll work heart and soul to restore the team’s pride.” Starting with two away trips Vieira’s time in charge of Senegal coincides with the international retirement of long-serving first-choice goalkeeper Edouard Mendy Vieira has been thrust straight into competitive action in qualifiers for the 2027 Afcon with two fixtures in this international window, two more in November and the final two rounds in March 2027. His stint in charge was due to begin with a home match against Mozambique on Friday, 25 September but the fixture has been reversed as Dakar is in the midst of preparations for the 2026 Youth Olympic Games . “Of course, I’d have preferred to play the first match here in Dakar but unfortunately, with the federation, we all felt the best decision was to postpone the match and go and play in Mozambique,” Vieira explained. “Those are difficulties we’re going to accept and deal with.” Senegal will be without several notable names for the trip to Maputo and the subsequent away game against Ethiopia on 29 September. Long-time number one Edouard Mendy, 34, has retired from Teranga Lions duty and Vieira said talismanic forward Sadio Mane will be absent with “a bit of a physical issue”. Despite previous speculation that Mane, also 34, could follow Mendy into retirement, Vieira said the former Liverpool and Bayern Munich man will “surely” be part of his next selection, fitness permitting. Right-back Krepin Diatta has been left out because he is currently without a club, while forward Ismaila Sarr, who is yet to feature for Crystal Palace this season because of transfer speculation and a groin injury, is also absent. ‘No doubt’ about his managerial ability Vieira’s most recent managerial role was at Genoa but he was sacked in November 2025 after a poor start to the Serie A season Vieira’s career as a player was trophy-laden but he has found the same kind of success hard to come by as a manager. He departed Palace in March 2023 with a record of 22 wins from 74 games in all competitions and, after a season at Strasbourg, has been out of work since being sacked by Genoa in November last year with the Italian club bottom of the table. He had guided them to safety in Serie A in the 2024-25 campaign but was then dismissed after six defeats in nine league games at the start of last season. “When you talk about my coaching career, or a certain amount of experience, I’ve always been someone who stays positive,” Vieira said. “That means you learn, and there are always positive things to take from it. I’m a better coach today than I was in my last spell at Genoa, because that experience helped me grow and made me realise certain things. “Given the experience I have as a manager, I’ve got no doubt about my ability to meet the expectations of fans.” Vieira was warmly received when he arrived in Dakar on Thursday evening, with video clips posted on social media showing him holding a Senegal flag aloft while shaking hands with a throng of fans gathered at the capital’s airport. “I couldn’t have been given a warmer welcome. I saw the supporters’ enthusiasm and I thank them for it. “Taking charge of this national team isn’t just a new stage in my career – it’s coming back home.”

items.title: Harry and Meghan’s media treatment echoes what happened to Diana, Earl Spencer tells BBC
items.description: Earl Spencer has told the BBC that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex’s treatment at the hands of the media has “echoes” of what happened to his sister Diana, Princess of Wales. He described press coverage of Prince Harry and Meghan as a “cancerous influence in their life” and said it would be “beholden on people to learn from Diana’s example”. The Sussexes, who recently returned to the UK from California six years after stepping back from royal duties, have been repeatedly critical of the media. It comes after the BBC reported on Friday that Earl Spencer says he was “telling the truth” when he claimed King Charles said people would forget Diana “soon enough” in a phone call in the days after her death . Speaking to Laura Kuenssberg at his Althorp estate, Earl Spencer was asked if he believed Diana would “identify” with the scrutiny the Duke and Duchess of Sussex face. “If you look at an article in a tabloid about Diana or the couple that you were mentioning, Harry and Meghan, you know, they can be really, really unpleasant,” he replied. “And I think it would be really beholden on people to learn from Diana’s example. “I’m not here to speak for Harry and Meghan, but for anyone who’s being destroyed in this way daily, it must be such a cancerous influence in their life.” He said he saw Diana’s “tears of despair” when describing the impact of media coverage on her, adding she was “very, very sensitive to criticism”. Earl Spencer said his sister -who married the then-Prince Charles in 1981- was “really brought low by all that criticism”, describing it as a “pity” to see “echoes of that now” in the treatment of his nephew Prince Harry and wife Meghan. He also said he thought there was a media perception that he was “on Harry’s side” but insisted: “I’m on my deceased sister’s sons’ side, both of them and if either of them wanted anything, then I’d be equally there for them.” Princess Diana was subject to huge press interest right up until her death in a car crash in Paris on 31 August 1997. In the eulogy he delivered at her funeral, Earl Spencer accused the media of being on a “permanent quest…to bring her down” and said newspapers had been threatened by her “genuine goodness”. Princess Diana: My Sister’s Story. The full interview with Laura Kuenssberg will be on BBC iPlayer on Sunday from 16:00 BST and on BBC One at 18:30 BST His comments about the Sussexes come just weeks after the pair returned to the UK. They have long been critical of their treatment by the British press and of the support they received from the Royal Family prior to their decision to leave the UK. In the couple’s 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey, Prince Harry accused the tabloid media of creating a “toxic environment” of “control and fear”. Meghan, meanwhile, said in the couple’s 2022 Netflix series that “no matter how hard I tried, no matter how good I was, no matter what I did, they [the media] were still going to find a way to destroy me”. In July this year, Prince Harry and six others, including Liz Hurley and Sir Elton John, lost a privacy case against the publisher of the Daily Mail, and may face a legal bill of up to £34.5m. In separate, earlier legal battles, the Duke of Sussex beat the Mirror Group in court, and the News Group out of court, forcing a settlement, damages, payout and apology. Earl Spencer’s interview with the BBC was his first since the Palace issued a strongly worded response to his claims about King Charles. That statement said the King was “mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgement and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss”. Earl Spencer, in comments first reported on Friday, reacted to it by saying: “Well, is he furious? Is he furious or is he embarrassed?” He added: “I’ve only ever had two calls on the line with Prince Charles at any stage of my life. “I was hyper alert to what he was saying and those are precisely the words that he said and I promise that to you now. Genuinely, that is what he said. I don’t hear him saying he didn’t say that.” Pressed on whether he had evidence to back up the claim, he said he told family and friends at the time what had been said “because it was so monstrous”. In his response to the Palace disputing his account, Earl Spencer, who shares his first name with the King, said: “They’ve sort of smudged that one, haven’t they? They’ve said that recollections may vary.” When asked which Charles the public was meant to believe, he said: “I’m telling the truth.” Speaking to the Mail on Sunday, Earl Spencer accused the King of psychological manipulation over the palace’s statement. “It is not every day you wake up to find you’ve been gaslit by the King,” he said. “It was astonishingly provocative and below the belt because it was essentially trying to say I’d lied without the King being able to deny what I’d said”. Journalist Richard Kay, who had been close friends with Diana, also wrote in the newspaper on Sunday that in the week between her death and funeral, Earl Spencer had told him of a “furious row” with Charles. “It was ‘about the boys’, but he was reluctant to go further,” said Kay, adding that Earl Spencer said the then prince had been “utterly pathetic”. However, speaking to BBC Radio 4’s Broadcasting House on Sunday, Dame Julia Cleverdon, a trusted aide and friend of the King, said the claims about his response to Diana’s death did not reflect “the language or the behaviours of a man I’ve known for 40 years”. Earl Spencer’s book, Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, is due to be published next week and is expected to be highly critical of the Royal Family. In further extracts published on Thursday, he claimed how the King “sounded giddily elated” when he called him after Diana’s death, alleging Charles sounded like a “lottery winner”. Dame Julia said: “To say that the Prince of Wales was elated and somehow took any pleasure… he was as if a 10-tonne truck had fallen on him. Her own husband had died a fortnight before Diana and she said Charles “could not have been more supportive, loving, concerned about the children and interested”.

items.title: The thematic response of Izonebi Alfred and Tompolo’s Haulers and Hailers
items.description: By Gogi Serikoromo Purely in a historically anticipatory celebration of scholarship, friendship, Tompology, and Dr. Enewaridideke Ekanpou’s books, Tompolo’s Haulers and Hailers and The Wanted Man in Camp Four, the exceptionally gifted Ijaw highlife musician JKing Dr. Izonebi Alfred has once again emerged in public discourse. This emergence in public discourse is foregrounded by the fact that Dr. Alfred, who is poised to go to London for a cultural fiesta in September 2026, has made an anticipatory acquisition of 200 copies of Dr. Enewaridideke Ekanpou’s new books, Tompolo’s Haulers and Hailers and The Wanted Man in Camp Four. In this expressed anticipatory journey to the world of books, Dr. Alfred is stirred by the thematic relevance of these books, which dwell on environmental advocacy, moral re-orientation, the Niger Delta struggle for developmental transformation, advocacy against pipeline vandalism and crude oil theft, and the crude and false propaganda machinery mounted against the current war against pipeline vandalism and crude oil theft in Nigeria. The purpose of this anticipatory acquisition of 200 copies of Tompolo’s Haulers and Hailers and The Wanted Man in Camp Four is to ensure the availability of these books in every home. The far-sighted Dr. Alfred sees this as a guarantee for the sustainability of the Niger Delta struggle in every generation, even after ages—when these books are generously given out to people to read and imbibe the ideas embedded in them. For Dr. Alfred, the fact that the books chronicle the Niger Delta struggle right from its inception, highlighting the patriotic roles of Isaac Boro, Tompolo, and others, naturally recommends them as valuable materials for every Niger Deltan who needs the history of the Niger Delta struggle. In other words, it makes them sufficiently awakened to the realities in their environment and enables them to make informed decisions on how to cope with the emerging challenges in life in relation to the Niger Delta struggle for developmental freedom and comfort. To historically broaden the horizons of Niger Deltans as regards the Niger Delta struggle and to prepare them for the struggle ahead without resort to violence, Dr. Alfred has decided to acquire 200 copies of Dr. Ekanpou’s Tompolo’s Haulers and Hailers and The Wanted Man in Camp Four to be distributed to people. Dr. Alfred holds the view that generously giving out 200 copies of these books to the public would help in the formation and germination of the right attitudes and values with regard to the Niger Delta struggle. By this approach, this generation and the next generation of Niger Deltans would be adequately awakened to the icons of the Niger Delta struggle and the respectable attitude to be adopted towards the icons of the Niger Delta struggle. In the thinking of the Ijaw music legend, Dr. Alfred, the generous distribution of these 200 copies to people in cities and villages would inculcate in the younger generation the culture of giving respect to the icons of the Niger Delta struggle, particularly High Chief Government Ekpemupolo (Tompolo) and his iconic contemporaries in the Niger Delta struggle. Dr. Alfred maintains that the intellectually channelled education and enlightenment embedded in Dr. Ekanpou’s Tompolo’s Haulers and Hailers and The Wanted Man in Camp Four would put an end to the cascade of disparaging false narratives impetuously carved around the icons of the Niger Delta struggle, particularly High Chief Tompolo and his patriotic activities in Nigeria. For Dr. Alfred, his acquired 200 books would be shared with the public without discrimination in any community he would be engaged to entertain. Clearly, Dr. Alfred’s acquisition of 200 copies of Tompolo’s Haulers and Hailers and The Wanted Man in Camp Four, to be shared with the public as a philanthropic gesture on the intellectual front, underscores his historic commitment to the Niger Delta struggle beyond the music plane of engagement for which he has been known for decades. This pragmatic educational investment in this generation and the unborn generations, through the anticipatory acquisition and giving out of 200 copies of Tompolo’s Haulers and Hailers and The Wanted Man in Camp Four, is a highly commendable gesture which must be applauded by every generation, particularly this generation. Dr. Alfred has historically become the iconic musician whose interest in a better society transcends his known music world of spellbinding performances on the stage. items.title: Kpélé / troubles liés à l’usage des substances psychoactives : Des responsables de formations sanitaires éclairés
items.description: Adéta, 20 sept, (ATOP) – Des responsables de formations sanitaires de la préfecture de Kpélé ont pris part à une formation sur la prévention et la prise en charge des personnes atteintes de troubles liés à l’usage des substances psychoactives les 18 et 19 septembre à Adéta. Cette formation est initiée par le ministère de la Santé, de l’Hygiène publique, de la Couverture sanitaire universelle et des Assurances avec l’appui technique et financier de l’Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS). Elle s’inscrit dans le cadre d’un briefing destiné aux participants et dans l’alignement des orientations nationale et régionales. Il s’est agi de renforcer leurs compétences, afin d’améliorer la prévention, l’identification et la prise en charge intégrée des troubles liés à l’usage des substances psychoactives. Les bénéficiaires de cette formation ont été éclairés sur les troubles liés à l’usage des substances, le traitement, la récupération et le rôle des professionnels de soutien à la récupération. Ils ont également acquis des connaissances sur les compétences de base et les activités de ces professionnels, la gestion des situations difficiles dans le processus de récupération, l’auto – soin, ainsi que sur la prévention des traumatismes secondaires. L’administrateur de programme des maladies non transmissibles à l’OMS, Dr Komivi Mawusi Aho a insisté sur l’engagement des bénéficiaires pour modifier profondément le caractère, le comportement ou l’état physique et moral des consommateurs des substances psychoactives. Ils les ont exhortés à appliquer les acquis de la formation pour améliorer la qualité des soins et organiser des séances de sensibilisation dans les établissements scolaires et aussi dans les communautés pour prévenir l’usage des substances psychoactives. Le directeur préfectoral de la santé de Kpélé, Dr Mensavi Amblasso a invité les participants à mettre à profit cette formation pour réduire le fardeau de l’addition de substances psychoactives dans la préfecture. Il a témoigné sa gratitude au gouvernement et à l’OMS pour leur engagement dans la promotion d’une meilleure santé à tous les Togolais. ATOP/SKD/AR/KYA

items.title: Nvidia boss rejects AI extinction fears as ‘doomsday narratives’
items.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has described warnings that AI could lead to humanity’s extinction by the next decade as “doomsday narratives”. “2030 is not going to be the end of the world. There is 0% chance that’s going to be the end of the world”, Huang said in an interview with CBS News, the BBC’s US partner. Huang added: “Scaring people is unnecessary. It is irresponsible.” Warnings from researchers in recent weeks about potential risks posed by the technology escalated the debate about AI safety, with some industry executives calling for a slowdown in developing models. His remarks follow claims posted on social media by former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon that AI developers believe the technology “could kill us all by the end of the decade”. Coxon’s concerns sparked debate about the technology’s risks, including calls by top executives like Anthropic boss Dario Amodei and OpenAI’s Sam Altman urging for AI’s development to slow down. Huang said that such predictions are “not grounded in science”, adding that it is in Nvidia’s best interest to ensure the industry builds its products responsibly. “Our company’s success is directly connected to the safe deployment of products and services,” he said. “If we don’t continue to do that, our value would be diminished.” Huang suggested AI firms talking about a “slow down” could be seeking liability protections for harms their products may cause. “Go and read between the lines,” he said. “They’re actually not asking for more laws. They’re asking to be relieved of the laws we do have, and I think that that’s a problem.” Nvidia is a key player in the industry, developing cutting edge computer chips that are crucial for making AI models. The firm’s most powerful chips face restrictions in China due to measures imposed by both Washington and Beijing. US export controls aim to slow China’s military and AI progress, while Chinese regulations are designed to encourage reliance on domestically produced technology. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng held talks in New York on Sunday as they try to strike deals on AI, tariffs and critical minerals. The meeting came as President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are due to hold a summit in Washington later this week. Last week, Huang appeared at a UK summit hosted by King Charles , who warned tech leaders of the “existential dangers” of AI. “The task before you is not merely to advance technology, but to ensure that it remains firmly in the service of humanity, community and the natural world,” the King told the group. In the US, President Donald Trump has downplayed concerns about AI’s risks . Trump made a surprise phone call to Huang while the Nvidia boss was speaking on stage at a tech conference in Los Angeles on 14 September. During the call, Trump criticised calls to slow the pace of AI development and dismissed fears as a “hoax”.

items.title: Edo council boss redeems N20m pledge to soldier’s family
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — The Chairman of Etsako East Local Government Area and Chairman of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria (ALGON), Edo State, Hon. Sunny Ekpeson, has redeemed his N20 million pledge to the family of late Lance Corporal Fahad Sani of the 195 Battalion, Nigerian Army, Agenebode. Sani died on July 2, 2026, following a road accident along the Okpella Highway while returning from a rescue operation. The late soldier and his colleagues had reportedly responded to a distress call involving kidnapped victims in the bushes of Okpella and successfully rescued them. However, tragedy struck on their return when a speeding trailer reportedly rammed into the vehicle conveying the soldiers. Following the incident, Ekpeson, who was then Acting Chairman of Etsako East LGA, visited the bereaved family and pledged N20 million to support Sani’s wife and their two young children. He redeemed the pledge at a presentation ceremony attended by members of the deceased’s family and personnel of the 195 Battalion, led by its Commanding Officer, Major S.D. Balafama. Balafama commended Ekpeson for fulfilling his promise, describing the gesture as a source of encouragement to the bereaved family and the battalion. He said the support demonstrated that the sacrifice of Sani and other personnel serving the country was recognised. The Commanding Officer also appreciated Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, for what he described as his continued support for security agencies and families of fallen personnel. Speaking at the ceremony, Ekpeson said honouring fallen heroes should go beyond words, stressing that personnel who risked their lives to protect citizens should not be forgotten after their death. He said the N20 million package was structured to provide long-term support for the family. According to him, part of the money would enable the deceased’s wife to establish a sustainable business, while N10 million would be placed in a fixed deposit account to support the education and future needs of their two children. “The gesture is intended to ensure that the sacrifice made by the late soldier in the service of the nation will continue to have a positive impact on his family,” Ekpeson said. items.title: The president versus us
items.description: By Tony Afejuku Let the Glitterer state straightaway that today’s subject is appearing for readers’ consumption by sheer luck. What this simply means is that the Glitterer had other things in his mind, of active choices to choose from, before a nudge from nowhere nudged him to pick, prettily, on our president directly now. Let the Glitterer be clearly clear. He legitimately had in his sumptuously active mind the following topics to dwell on: “Other stories and a story”; “New hunger in the land”; “The thing that is the thing to come”; “An insider glimpse of Olu of Warri’s fifth coronation anniversary”; “The funny humourist”; “Infantino”; “World Cup of woeful dreams”; and other ideas of almost perceptible and almost imperceptible ingredients. As a matter of fact, “Other stories and a story”, which was going to attend to the responses of some readers, active readers, of this column, was ready to be shared here from their intellectual and poetic insights. Its lucky day, and that of the other titles, will still enter the creatively journalistic soul of the Glitterer. During a rare, favoured moment of this presidency, our leader elevated his presence to enter the Glitterer’s mind of dark humour and bile, catching the Glitterer utterly unready for the cynicism skulking there. This rare, lucky moment happened very recently when some Nigerian Catholic Bishops visited the president, our mighty leader, to tell him that the country is bleeding. Did our mighty leader accept the truth the Bishops, led by Cardinal John Onaiyekan, the Archbishop Emeritus of Abuja, told him? Of course, the President of Nigeria, the great man of gambit, did not agree with the Bishops. The bleeding country is already being throttled to the un-motorable road of a one-party state, which our lucky leader tried to deny outright against the grain of truth all about us. Without doubt, there is more than an adequate account/amount – if the Glitterer must employ this term – of hunger everywhere about us. Indeed, the failures, the current ingredients of failures, that is, of our serious leader’s administration, overwhelm us all. Let us attempt to list them: steadily rising inflation; frequent fuel price hikes; power failure; increasing poverty; declining education standards; increasing insecurity; economic downturn; debt increase; naira devaluation; and contrived democracy of a confirmed democrat drawing us backward. In other words, the Glitterer is saying thus: The structural failures characterizing the current administration have created an overwhelming national crisis. This is evident in persistent inflation, escalating fuel costs, systemic power grid failures, and expanding poverty rates. These economic challenges are compounded by a decline in educational quality, heightened insecurity, mounting sovereign debt, and the continuous devaluation of the naira. Consequently, the administration’s governance model represents a regression in democratic substance. The president and his presidencynologists will not agree with me, as the president himself did not agree with the Catholic Bishops who (through Cardinal John Onaiyekan) spoke for all of us Catholics and non-Catholics, Christians and non-Christians, and all of us Nigerians who keep on wondering about the luckless luck that has befallen Nigeria currently. But I don’t wish to be misunderstood. When President Tinubu’s gambit propelled him to the presidency in 2023, did we deduce that we would witness what we are experiencing now – as alluded to above? Of course not! This must be our collective answer. Now when the Glitterer saw our leader of enormous power on television, and heard what he said, to wit, that all is fair in politics, he winced with pain. The powerful president’s statement, meaning any tactic is acceptable to win the 2027 presidential elections, really caused the Glitterer deep emotional pain and a sudden, nameless dread. And his mind spiralled into anxiety as he foresaw a dark, chaotic, and unclear future surrounding the upcoming 2027 presidential elections. In any case, will the elections happen? And if they happen, will they be the elections of the president versus his opponents, or will they be the elections of the president versus the rest of us? This composer may not be losing faith in the presidential electorate and electoral process, although he believes that, after all is said and done, all Nigerian (and African) politicians in a post-colonial state such as ours are more or less the same. Our past presidents lived and survived/succeeded in office by wits. Is our powerfully powerful President Tinubu different from them? Or will his unlikely civilian successor be going to be different? Have our experiences over the years not told us that our presidents have exhibited tendencies to make one civilian president sound a bit like the other? Or is the current President of your country, my country, our country, going to step into his peculiar bog hole as the 2027 presidential elections approach? Now the Glitterer wants to make a recommendation. There are occasions when he is like every writer. He begins a sentence, runs to the middle of it, and discovers that there is no way out short of retracing his steps and beginning again nicely and beautifully. We expect the presidencynologists to read this writing, and have a dialogue with the president on it. All of us will be lucky if they do so. It is morning yet on 2027 presidential elections day. The president of presidents still has ample time to kill the hunger in the land. Or did his gambit bring him to his present throne to bleed us to death? Who will remain in the land to rule over it after he has killed us all? It is morning yet on 2027 presidential election day. His gambit still has time to wear a humane heart and face. He should heed the Glitterer. He cannot conquer and consume all of us – even if he can conquer and consume the presidential candidates who want our presidential throne. Mr Powerful President of presidents should rewrite his sentences. The post The president versus us appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Schools Concession: The Ministry of Education as a retarded child, by Owei Lakemfa
items.description: A country’s Ministry of Education is supposed to be a place of illumination with clear ideas about the future. Nigeria has had not just super educators like Professors Wole Soyinka, Ebi Alagoa, Alvan Ikoku and Adamu Baikie, but also outstanding Education Ministers like Abudu Yusufu Eke and Babs Fafunwa. The ongoing conflagration over the award of King’s College, KC, Lagos, to a group of its Old Boys again exposes the current leadership of the Education Ministry under Dr Tunji Maruf Alausa as retarded. Before analysing the KC issue, permit me to address this issue of incompetence in the Education Ministry. I have made this point about the Ministry a number of times, including in its clumsy and profligate attempts to auction 33 hectares of the Federal Government College, Kano, school land. In my May 2026 column titled ‘Minister Alausa: Little Learning Is Dangerous’, I pointed out that the Tinubu administration’s attempt to cut courses in the social sciences and arts because they allegedly do not lead to employment is illiterate and anti-intellectual. Also, in my July 6, 2026 column, ‘When Uneducated Minds Change the Education System’, I pointed out that, without consultations, the Ministry had, on September 3, 2025, ordered a major review of our national education curriculum. Then, just nine months later, the same Ministry, under the same Minister in the same Tinubu administration, announced that it was replacing the 6-3-3-4 education system with a linear 12-year one, exposing the administration’s lack of strategic and long-term thinking on education, which is the bedrock of development. As I write, some of our universities are in turmoil, with a number of them on strike over non-payment of agreed allowances in public universities. But the administration, with Alausa as its arrowhead, is already sowing the seeds for the next round of crisis in the education sector. The National Universities Commission, NUC Act (Cap. N81 and Section E3 of the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004), vests in the NUC the sole authority to lay minimum standards using the Benchmark Minimum Academic Standards, BMAS, under which all universities must operate. It is also empowered to accredit academic awards in the country and evaluate programmes through peer-review panels, which inspect institutional facilities, curricula and staffing. Equally, the NUC is empowered to withhold or withdraw approval of academic programmes and exercise supremacy over professional degrees. As far as I know, the NUC has not been found wanting, nor have the laws been reviewed. But the Tinubu administration, on Wednesday, September 9, 2026, decided to establish a parallel accreditation body, baptised the ‘Ministerial Committee’. If there are no ulterior motives, the administration ought to have told the country in what way the NUC might be failing, consulted stakeholders like the Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, and, if necessary, reviewed the relevant laws. But to set up a parallel body amounts to illegality. Now, to the KC issue. The least expected of an Education Ministry is to educate and inform the public on any major issue it embarks on. But it is in this basic faculty that the Ministry is found wanting. Either because it has an inept and incapable leadership or a mischievous one imbued with a rogue mentality, it does not even engage in basic consultation with those its policies may affect. For instance, it decided to hand over the management and administration of the 117-year-old KC to a group in the school’s Old Boys’ Association without consultations. This group of investors is empowered to impose fees, control teachers, make a profit on their so-called investment or, at least, break even. So, rather than being a social product, KC becomes a commodity that can be traded. Needless to say, the new investors, even if they pretend to grant some scholarships, would eventually price the school out of the reach of the poor, even the middle class. These Old Boys are likely to put a high price on an education and school that gave them free education. In any case, if these men are so interested in education or making positive contributions, why can’t they establish their own school rather than seek to take over a school with a good pedigree? The KC case raises another question. Can Old Boys administer medicine to an allegedly sick alma mater without adding poison? Given my experience with the Methodist Boys’ High School, Lagos Old Boys’ Association, MBHS OBA, the answer is yes! In the MBHS case, while the state government handed the school primarily to the mission, the Old Boys provided virtually every other facility, including teachers’ quarters, an assembly hall, a library, laboratories and water. Yet, we did not attempt to seize the school. We made, and are still making, all these contributions because the school provided us with the basic foundations that made us who we are today. If there are no ulterior motives, why is the KC agreement shrouded in secrecy? Why were critical stakeholders, such as the students who will bear the brunt, their parents and guardians who will be forced to pay, the teachers whose careers as public servants may be jeopardised, and the unions and professional associations whose members will be affected, not consulted? Why were their inputs not sought? If the government claims it wants the best for the school and concession is the best option, why not make it open? Why must the school be handed to a set of people who may not have the professional competence to run it? This move is nothing but racketeering. The prime land of the school is also an attraction. But I must admit that this prodigal trajectory did not start with the Tinubu administration. In 2006, the Obasanjo administration, with Dr Oby Ezekwesili as Education Minister, embarked on this same path. It wanted to hand over the Federal Government Colleges to private administrators and managers. There are, however, some remarkable differences between the two administrations. While Obasanjo, despite his military background, engaged in wide consultations, Tinubu, in spite of his pro-democracy credentials, did not engage in consultations. He simply decided to impose his will. Again, while Obasanjo backed away, Tinubu, as he did when he announced the immediate removal of the oil subsidy, simply handed the KC over. The pushback we are witnessing is not his re-reading of the situation, but the resistance he is facing from stakeholders. Generally, education is not a commercial commodity to be bought and sold in the marketplace. Rather, it is a social vehicle to develop society. So, in educating our citizens, we are not doing them a favour; we are doing ourselves a favour. My advice is that the Tinubu administration should concentrate on mass education, especially of the 20 million out-of-school children. I come in peace. The post Schools Concession: The Ministry of Education as a retarded child, by Owei Lakemfa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Workers came across human remains – and unearthed a mass grave of 572 people
items.description: When a mass grave was unearthed in northern Sri Lanka last February, it was not by design. Workers were digging to extend a cremation ground in the Chemmani area of the Jaffna region when they suddenly discovered human remains, prompting an investigation. By August, archaeologists had completed the third phase of the excavation at the site, during which they found the skeletal remains of 572 people, including children and infants. Among the dead were artefacts from their lives – bangles, a school bag, a milk bottle. It is believed to be the largest mass grave site ever uncovered in Sri Lanka. There had been whispers of its existence before – a soldier on trial for the rape and murder of a young woman during the country’s devastating civil war, had spoken about a mass grave which contained hundreds of bodies. Rights groups said they were disappeared civilians But there was no proof – until now. And while the discovery is devastating, it has offered hope to people like Jeyaruby Jeyabalan, whose father was among thousands of people who disappeared during the decades-long war. Jeyabalan and families like his hope that answers about what happened to their loved ones lie among the bodies. Many Tamils believe the grave holds the victims of extrajudicial killings carried out during the civil war. They are calling for an investigation – and for justice. But the excavation process at Chemmani has moved slowly, testing the patience of families searching for answers about their disappeared loved ones. The discovery of hundreds of remains near a previously identified mass grave has fuelled anger among the Tamils, who have long-demanded a thorough inquiry into disappearances. Many fear the mass grave will eventually fade from public attention because of a lack of political will to pursue the truth – and so the grave has become a rallying point for renewed protests in Sri Lanka’s north. Two decades waiting for answers Sri Lanka, particularly the Tamil-dominated north and east, suffered decades of conflict. The war, which lasted from 1983 to 2009, divided the island-nation along ethnic lines. Tamil Tiger rebels fought for an independent state in the north-east of the country due to what they called systematic discrimination by the Sinhalese-dominated government. The conflict lasted 26 years and the fighting killed an estimated 100,000 people. It also left about 23,000 – mostly Tamils – missing. Both the security forces and Tamil Tigers are accused of atrocities and crimes . A baby’s bottle was among the personal items uncovered at the grave site. In 1995, after a bloody conflict, the Sri Lankan army wrested control of the Jaffna Peninsula from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE). It was seen as a key turning point in the war, which ended with the defeat of the Tigers in 2009. As they extended control in the late 1990s, the entire Chemmani region became part of a high-security zone and was dotted with army camps, check points and security posts. There was an army camp in Chemmani close to the cemetery as well. Some at that time described the Jaffna region as an “open prison” – and the security forces were accused of causing the disappearance of thousands of civilians, something Sri Lankan governments have always denied. “I was 12 years old when my father was picked up by the Sri Lankan army at a checkpoint close to Chemmani area in September 1996. We still don’t know what happened to him,” Jeyaruby Jayapalan, who now lives in Jaffna, tells the BBC. She recalls how, after learning of his disappearance, the family panicked and visited military camps and police stations across Jaffna in a desperate search for information without any luck. He never came back. Her father, Kandaiah Jayapalan, was a government employee who also ran a roadside café not far from Chemmani. “I went to Chemmani mass grave with many others hoping that I will find some answers. But we didn’t find any material evidence. We want a detailed forensic analysis of the human remains,” says Jeyaruby. Two weeks before Kandaiah Jayapalan vanished, an 18-year-old Tamil school girl, Krishanthi Kumaraswamy, disappeared in the same area. In 1998, a court in Colombo sentenced five soldiers to death for the rape and murder of Kumaraswamy and for killing three of her family members. The case drew global attention at that time. Their bodies were later found buried in Chemmani area . It is among the most infamous cases from the conflict – and the grave currently under investigation is within 100 metres of the remains of Kumaraswamy and others were found. In a startling court testimony, one of the convicted soldiers, Somaratne Rajapakse, alleged that between 300 and 400 people who had been killed in the mid-1990s were buried in Chemmani. His claim led to the first excavation at Chemmani a year later, during which investigators unearthed more than 10 human skeletons. Human rights activists believed those remains were linked to people who had disappeared during the civil war, but there was little judicial follow-up. Activists say that because the war with the Tamil rebels was ongoing, the then government didn’t pursue the investigation and did not explain why. The discovery of another mass grave in the same area has revived calls for accountability. Map of Sri Lanka showing location of Chemmani “Preliminary inspections suggest this was not a normal burial site and not consistent with ordinary Hindu burial practices,” says Gehan Gunatilleke, a commissioner with Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka, which conducted inspections at Chemmani last year. Activists and experts say that while a few dozen bodies appeared to have been formally buried, the vast majority told a different story. Most of the human remains were found without clothing, packed tightly together and, in some cases, stacked on top of others. The graves were shallow, with bodies buried just one to two metres below the surface. “There is a reasonable likelihood that the burials were unlawful and pursuant to extrajudicial killings,” the Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka said in a report last year. Past investigations haven’t led to prosecutions The families of those disappeared during the conflict have responded to the discovery by holding protest meetings and remembrance ceremonies. Among them is Suseela, a 65-year-old woman who is looking for her son, Gnanaseelan Ravi, who was picked up by the Sri Lankan military in 2007, when he was 24. “He was my only son, and I keep crying every day remembering him. My life is empty without him,” she tells the BBC. She went to Chemmani grave but couldn’t find any evidence, likes clothes or personal jewellery, that suggested her son was buried there. DNA tests on the human remains are yet to be carried out. All the remains recovered so far from Chemmani have been kept in the Forensic Department of the University of Jaffna campus under court custody. “We are preparing an interim report, and it will be submitted to the court by the end of September,” Prof Raj Somadeva, the chief archaeologist of the mass grave told the BBC. Some of the samples are expected to be sent abroad for detailed examination to help determine the age of the remains. Separate medical analyses will be needed to establish the possible causes of death. More than 20 mass graves have been found across Sri Lanka in recent decades, but none have been conclusively linked to enforced disappearances or alleged extra-judicial killings in the north and south of the country – and none have led to prosecutions. Given the failure of the authorities to investigate previous mass graves, there is scepticism among many Tamil people over what the new investigation might achieve. They point out to the outcome of the investigation on another mass grave was unearthed in the north-western town of Mannar in 2018 in which more than 350 skeletal remains were found. Investigations proved inconclusive, leaving many families disappointed. They want Sri Lanka to be referred to the International Criminal Court. The government of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake insists that it is fully cooperating with the investigation. Suseela holds a photograph of her son, Gnanaseelan Ravi, who was picked up by the Sri Lankan military in 2007, when he was 24. After coming to power in September 2024, Dissanayake promised to work towards justice and ethnic reconciliation. But his government vehemently opposes any international mechanism to investigate alleged war crimes committed during the ethnic conflict, disappointing Tamils. “We will continue with the excavation work at Chemmani,” Harshana Nanayakkara, Sri Lanka’s justice minister told the BBC. “We need to analyse the skeletons and find out how these people died. Then we have to carry out DNA tests,” he said. The government, he insists, has also asked the families to give their DNA so that it can be analysed later with the remains. During his inspection at Chemmani in June, the minister promised investigations to find justice and truth to bring an end to the matter. He also promised that necessary funding will be allocated for the excavation. The Sri Lankan army spokesman, Brigadier Waruna Gamage rejects allegations that security forces buried civilians after massacring them. “All the allegations should be proved in court,” he told the BBC. Calls for international assistance Families of the disappeared are protesting, demanding international investigation into Chemmani mass grave. The delays in investigating past crimes have attracted stringent criticism from rights groups. After years of international pressure, in 2018 the government set up an independent body, the Office of the Missing Persons (OMP), to investigate the disappearances. But those affected say it hasn’t made much progress in finding their missing relatives. “Many cases of forced disappearance, torture and killing remain stalled, while families of victims and human rights defenders face threats and intimidation,” Human Rights Watch said in a report earlier this month. The United Nations has urged Sri Lanka to seek international help in identifying the victims, to find out how they died, and who is responsible. “This is a situation where victims are deeply frustrated, have lived with pain for decades, have come to distrust past investigations,” Rory Mungoven, the Asia-Pacific chief at the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights tells the BBC. “I think involving international assistance would help to bolster confidence in these investigations,” he points out. Successive Sri Lankan governments have strongly resisted calls for international investigations into alleged wartime atrocities. During earlier reporting trips to Sri Lanka, I met parents and family members of the disappeared who campaigned for decades to the search for truth. Some have since passed away without ever discovering the fates of their loved ones . Human rights groups say that President Dissanayake’s government now has an opportunity to break from a long-standing pattern of delay and denial and deliver accountability for grave abuses committed during the conflict. Suseela is determined to know the truth. “I don’t know how long I will live with such uncertainty, but I want closure,” she says.

items.title: Législatives 2026: Aziz Akhannouch tacle l'opposition et fixe le cap pour 2026-2031
items.description: Devant une foule de plus de 13 000 personnes rassemblées à Tétouan dimanche soir dans le cadre de la campagne pour les élections législatives du 23 septembre, Aziz Akhannouch, ancien président du Rassemblement National des Indépendants (RNI) et membre de son bureau politique, a adressé un message cinglant à ceux qu'il a qualifiés de « faiseurs de promesses électorales », affirmant que leurs engagements sont « en contradiction avec la réalité, le terrain et leurs propres personnalités ». « Je ne parlerai pas des faiseurs de promesses, car au final, lorsqu'on analyse ce qu'ils promettent, on constate que c'est contradictoire. Contradictoire avec la réalité, avec le terrain, et même avec leurs propres personnalités », a déclaré Akhannouch. L'ancien président du parti de la « Colombe » s'est appuyé sur une métaphore footballistique évocatrice pour décrire la scène électorale : « Au début, je pensais qu'ils allaient nous amener un attaquant pour marquer des buts ; mais il s'est avéré qu'ils jouent en défense et que c'est vous qui marquez les buts. Vous marquez et les citoyens sont avec vous, vous marquez des buts parce que vous connaissez les préoccupations des Marocains et leurs aspirations. » Bilan gouvernemental Aziz Akhannouch est revenu sur le bilan du gouvernement actuel qu'il dirige, affirmant que l'équipe gouvernementale « a accompli un travail considérable ». Le chef du gouvernement a illustré son propos en évoquant la réforme du secteur de l'éducation, où le taux de généralisation des « Écoles pionnières » a atteint 80 %, en plus de la résolution définitive du dossier des enseignants contractuels. Dans le secteur de la santé, il a souligné le « doublement du budget qui lui est alloué ». Akhannouch a également abordé la revalorisation des salaires, avec une hausse de 1 000 dirhams octroyée à l'ensemble des fonctionnaires du secteur public, une augmentation du SMIG de 20 % et du SMAG de 25 %, ainsi que la revalorisation des traitements des médecins, des enseignants et des professeurs de l'enseignement supérieur. Il a ajouté que le gouvernement a mis en place l'aide au logement et lancé l'Aide sociale directe au profit de 4 millions de familles, tandis que le taux de généralisation de la couverture médicale a atteint 80 %, parallèlement au soutien du pouvoir d'achat, des transports et des éleveurs face aux années successives de sécheresse. Promesses pour l'avenir Abordant le « Programme des Indépendants 2026-2031 », Akhannouch a présenté les engagements de son parti pour la prochaine étape, annonçant notamment « une déduction fiscale de 5 000 dirhams pour les enfants scolarisés dans le secteur privé » parallèlement au parachèvement du déploiement des « Écoles pionnières », ainsi que le rehaussement du salaire minimum à 5 000 dirhams dans le cadre du dialogue social avec les partenaires économiques et sociaux. Le dirigeant du RNI a confirmé la volonté de sa formation d'optimiser l'indice de l'Aide sociale directe « au moment où certains veulent l'annuler », affirmant que le RNI souhaite « l'améliorer afin de renforcer l'autonomisation des familles vulnérables ». Il a également annoncé un « programme d'encouragement à l'épargne », à travers lequel l'État versera 25 dirhams pour chaque tranche de 100 dirhams épargnée par le citoyen, ainsi qu'un « plan de développement de l'intermédiation dans l’emploi visant la création d'un million d’emplois supplémentaires ». Tétouan, « source d'optimisme » Akhannouch a déclaré que le RNI clôture sa tournée nationale de meetings de campagne à Tétouan « parce que cette ville nous porte bonheur ». Il a souligné que la campagne « n'est pas encore terminée » et que « les candidats et militants resteront proches des citoyens durant les deux derniers jours précédant le 23 septembre ». Le responsable politique a exprimé ses remerciements aux militants du parti pour la « campagne mûre » qu'ils ont menée tout au long de la période écoulée, observant que les Marocains y ont « réagi favorablement ». Rappelant qu'il leur avait recommandé au début de la campagne d'« avancer avec sérénité », il a affirmé avoir constaté sur le terrain, dans les ruelles et les boulevards, qu'ils ont bénéficié d'un « grand accueil de la part des citoyens ». Concernant les deux jours restants, il a invité les militants à conserver leur calme, estimant que « la valeur d'un parti est déjà établie » et que « les choses ne changeront pas de manière spectaculaire au cours des 48 prochaines heures ». Dans une comparaison suggestive, Aziz Akhannouch a mis en parallèle l'engouement des campagnes électorales de 2021 et de 2026, rappelant qu'il présidait le parti en 2021 lorsque le RNI avait obtenu 2,1 millions de voix, tout en affirmant que l'enthousiasme de la campagne actuelle « était encore plus grand » qu'en 2021. Aziz Akhannouch a conclu son intervention en se disant confiant quant au soutien des Marocains envers les militants du parti, les lançant un appel : « Avancez avec confiance… avancez avec sérénité. » The post Législatives 2026: Aziz Akhannouch tacle l'opposition et fixe le cap pour 2026-2031 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: School resumption amid mounting insecurity
items.description: As the 2026/2027 school session begins across Nigeria, millions of parents face the familiar burdens of school fees, uniforms, books and transport. But for many, especially in conflict-prone communities, there is a more frightening question: will their children return home safely each day? The school, once regarded as a sanctuary of learning and hope, has increasingly become a target for terrorists and armed criminals whose abductions are traumatising families and threatening the future of education. The latest situation in Borno State is particularly disturbing. In Askira-Uba Local Government Area, about 80 pupils abducted during attacks on schools in Mussa and Lassa in May and June 2026 remain in captivity, according to local education authorities. Only 56 of the area’s 113 primary schools are currently functioning, with 57 shut because of insecurity. Some of the abducted children have now spent more than 100 days in captivity. The danger is not confined to the North-East. Schoolchildren in other parts of the country have also been targeted, demonstrating that criminal gangs are increasingly exploiting the vulnerability of educational institutions. This grim reality threatens to reverse whatever gains Nigeria has made in expanding access to education. Governments must therefore make school security an urgent national priority. The Safe Schools Initiative cannot remain a collection of commendable policies, committees and announcements. It must translate into visible protection. The Federal Government has announced stronger collaboration among education authorities, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, the police, the armed forces and intelligence agencies. What is required now is effective implementation, monitoring and accountability. Schools in vulnerable communities should have appropriate perimeter protection, controlled access, adequate lighting, emergency communication systems and clearly rehearsed evacuation procedures. More importantly, security agencies must maintain effective intelligence networks around schools and establish rapid-response arrangements with local communities. Existing school-safety intelligence and response mechanisms should be fully utilised rather than allowed to become another bureaucratic initiative. The criminal economy behind school abductions must also be dismantled. Kidnappers, informants, financiers and other facilitators who enable these crimes must face the full weight of the law. Every successful abduction emboldens criminals, enriches their networks and erodes parents’ confidence in the school system. Beyond the immediate security threat lies an even greater danger. Every school closed by insecurity creates room for illiteracy, child labour, exploitation, radicalisation and poverty to flourish. In communities already devastated by insurgency, prolonged school closures can produce a generation deprived of the opportunity to escape the cycle of violence and deprivation. As classrooms reopen, therefore, governments must understand that protecting schools is an investment in Nigeria’s future. No child should have to choose between education and personal safety. The new academic year must mark a renewed national determination to ensure that Nigerian schools remain places of learning, not hunting grounds for terrorists and kidnappers. Education must prevail over terror. The post School resumption amid mounting insecurity appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: LSE Listing: Dangote Cement makes global capital push in London
items.description: By Dapo Akinrefon Dangote Cement Plc will on September 21, take its growth and expansion story to the international capital market as it hosts a Capital Markets Day, CMD, in London, with investors expected to closely assess the Company’s expansion strategy, production capacity, African growth opportunities, capital allocation, profitability outlook and plans to sustain growth across its markets. The London engagement is part of preparations for the Company’s proposed secondary listing on the London Stock Exchange (LSE). It is expected to provide international investors and analysts with a deeper understanding of Dangote Cement’s business strategy, operations, financial performance, and medium- to long-term growth plans. The event, which will be held in London and streamed via webcast, will also provide an opportunity for investors to engage directly with the company’s senior management. Dangote Cement had on September 2, disclosed the planned investor engagement in a regulatory filing with the Nigerian Exchange (NGX), following shareholders’ approval of the proposed secondary listing. According to the company, the Capital Markets Day will provide investors and other stakeholders with an update on its strategy, operations and business priorities. The London investor engagement marks a significant step in Dangote Cement’s efforts to deepen its participation in international capital markets and broaden its investor base beyond Nigeria. The proposed LSE listing is expected to increase the Company’s visibility among global institutional investors and potentially widen its access to international capital, while complementing its existing listing on the NGX. The company is entering the London engagement on the back of strong financial performance in the first half of 2026, giving it a robust earnings story to present to international investors. For the six months ended June 30, 2026, Dangote Cement reported a 21.4 per cent year-on-year increase in group revenue to N2.51 trillion, while earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 25.8 per cent to N1.19 trillion. Profit after tax also increased by 22.7 per cent to N638.5 billion, compared with N520.5 billion recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The performance underscores the Company’s strong financial position as it engages global investors and sets out its medium- and long-term growth ambitions. Dangote Cement is Africa’s largest cement producer, with operations spanning 11 African countries and an installed production capacity of more than 55 million tonnes per annum. The company is listed on the Nigerian Exchange, where it remains one of the market’s largest and most closely followed stocks by institutional investors. Beyond the proposed LSE listing, tomorrow’s Capital Markets Day will place particular attention on how Dangote Cement intends to deploy capital, expand production, strengthen its African footprint and maintain profitability amid changing market conditions. The London event will therefore provide the company with a platform to present its investment proposition to the international capital market and position its African growth story ahead of the proposed secondary listing. items.title: FIA busts fake apostille network involving MoFA officials
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Investigation Agency’s (FIA) Anti-Corruption Circle Islamabad has busted a network allegedly involved in the preparation and use of fake apostille stickers in connivance with officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA). According to the FIA Islamabad Zone, the Anti-Corruption Circle carried out raids on multiple consultancy and courier offices in the basement of F&F Plaza, Aabpara, on the basis of credible information and unearthed a network allegedly involved in the preparation, delivery and use of fake apostille stickers, official seals and documents. A case has been registered against 22 accused under Sections 420, 468, 471 and 109 of the Pakistan Penal Code, read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. The investigation revealed that owners and employees of consultancy and courier firms, including Sophie Consultants, Excellent Courier Service, Leopard Courier Services at F&F Plaza, RAAK Consultancy, Noon Consultants (Pvt) Ltd, GM Consultants and Fair Line Service, were allegedly involved in the network. Six ministry officials, 16 private individuals nominated A total of 16 private individuals have been nominated in the case, along with six officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, including officials dealing with attestation and apostille matters. According to the FIA, the accused collected large sums from applicants on the pretext of expediting apostille and attestation services and allegedly bribed MoFA officials. The agency said fake apostille stickers had been circulating at various locations across the country, potentially causing losses to the national exchequer. A court has granted three-day physical remand of the arrested accused. The investigation is being conducted by Inspector Arsalan Masood Khan. Published in Dawn, September 21st, 2026

items.title: Each Jehovah’s Witness member now decides whether to accept or donate main blood components
items.description: The Governing Body of Jehovah’s Witnesses announced on Friday that the decision to accept red cells, white cells, plasma or platelets from another person’s blood is a matter of personal conscience. Likewise, each Witness must decide whether or not to donate blood for the clearly expressed purpose of providing components or fractions for use by another person. The long-standing refusal of whole-blood transfusions on religious grounds, a core teaching based on the command to ‘abstain from blood’ ( Acts 15:20 ), is unchanged. “Blood remains sacred to Jehovah’s Witnesses, who continue to regard life and blood as precious gifts from God,” Paul Gillies, international spokesman for Jehovah’s Witnesses at their World Headquarters, said. “We recognise that medical decisions involving blood components are a matter of conscience between each Witness and their God, Jehovah.” The adjustment follows earlier updates regarding blood fractions and the use of one’s own blood during medical procedures. Since the Bible does not comment on such decisions, they are a matter of individual conscience. That same reasoning has now been extended to the four main components of blood. Jehovah’s Witnesses love life and want the best available medical care. They do not practice faith healing, and they seek out doctors who can provide effective treatment in accord with their wishes, values and beliefs. “Congregations do not involve themselves in personal decisions that rest with the individual conscience. We will continue to respect and support the personal decisions of our fellow believers,” Mr. Gillies said. “We are grateful, too, for the many skilled and compassionate physicians who provide quality medical care that respects our personal wishes regarding blood.” Jehovah’s Witnesses number over nine million worldwide, in congregations across more than 200 lands.

Pouvoir d’achat, bilan gouvernemental et cohésion de la majorité : Bensaïd s’explique
items.description: À quelques jours des élections législatives de 2026, les tensions entre les composantes de la majorité gouvernementale alimentent le débat politique. Invité de l’émission La Route vers les élections 2026 sur Hespress , Mohamed Mehdi Bensaïd, ministre de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication et membre de la présidence collégiale du Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM), a rejeté les accusations selon lesquelles sa formation chercherait à se désolidariser du bilan du gouvernement auquel elle a participé durant cinq ans. © Mounir Mehimdate Le responsable du PAM a reconnu que son parti avait exprimé, au fil du mandat, des réserves sur certaines politiques publiques, notamment en matière de pouvoir d’achat, mais il estime que ces critiques relèvent du fonctionnement normal d’une coalition gouvernementale. « Nous ne nous sommes pas désolidarisés du bilan », a-t-il affirmé, rappelant que les partis de la majorité ont été confrontés à une succession de crises, dont la sécheresse et ses répercussions sur les prix des produits de première nécessité. Selon lui, ces circonstances ont conduit le PAM à formuler des propositions alternatives au sein des instances de coordination de la majorité. © Mounir Mehimdate Parmi ces propositions figurait notamment la création de sociétés régionales chargées de la distribution de produits alimentaires de base. « Nous avons porté cette idée à plusieurs reprises au sein de la majorité », a expliqué Bensaïd, estimant qu’elle aurait pu contribuer à limiter la hausse des prix qui affecte les ménages marocains depuis plusieurs années. Pour le ministre, la hausse des prix ne peut être dissociée des facteurs extérieurs, notamment le déficit pluviométrique et la flambée des cours du pétrole. Mais il considère que le rôle d’un parti social-démocrate est également de proposer des mécanismes d’intervention publique lorsque le pouvoir d’achat des citoyens est menacé. « Lorsqu’une crise touche directement les poches des Marocains, la conception de l’État social que nous défendons implique une intervention pour protéger un minimum acceptable pour les citoyens », a-t-il soutenu. © Mounir Mehimdate « La campagne électorale impose de parler du positif comme du négatif » Interrogé sur les critiques formulées par le PAM à l’encontre de certains résultats du gouvernement, alors même que le parti en est membre, Mehdi Bensaïd a revendiqué le droit de dresser un bilan nuancé à l’occasion de la campagne électorale. « Nous sommes aujourd’hui en campagne électorale. Nous avons le devoir de dire ce qui a fonctionné et ce qui n’a pas fonctionné », a-t-il déclaré, rejetant l’idée selon laquelle son parti devrait se contenter de défendre sans réserve l’action gouvernementale. Selon lui, les Marocains ont eux-mêmes constaté les limites de certaines politiques publiques, notamment celles destinées à soutenir le pouvoir d’achat. « L’État a déployé des moyens financiers importants, mais les résultats n’ont pas toujours été au rendez-vous », a-t-il affirmé, estimant que les interrogations sur l’efficacité de la gestion des aides publiques relèvent désormais des institutions compétentes. © Mounir Mehimdate Le dirigeant du PAM considère toutefois que ces critiques ne remettent pas en cause la solidarité gouvernementale. « Le rôle d’un parti dans une majorité n’est pas de dire que tout est parfait », a-t-il insisté. Pas de boycott du Conseil de gouvernement Mohamed Mehdi Bensaïd a également rejeté les accusations portant sur un prétendu boycott de la dernière réunion du Conseil de gouvernement par les ministres du PAM, accusation formulée notamment par Mohamed Aujjar, membre du bureau politique du Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI), lors d'une interview avec Hespress . « Il n’y a jamais eu de boycott », a assuré le ministre, rappelant que plusieurs membres du gouvernement issus du PAM étaient présents lors de cette réunion, parmi lesquels Abdellatif Ouahbi, Adib Benbrahim et Hicham Sabri. Les absences constatées s’expliqueraient, selon lui, par les contraintes liées à la campagne électorale et à d’autres engagements officiels. « Nous continuons à assumer nos responsabilités jusqu’à la dernière minute », a-t-il affirmé. © Mounir Mehimdate Défendre les réalisations tout en reconnaissant les insuffisances Le responsable politique a également rejeté l’idée selon laquelle le PAM chercherait à nier l’action menée durant le mandat. Il affirme au contraire que son parti défend les réalisations obtenues dans plusieurs secteurs tout en reconnaissant les insuffisances persistantes. Prenant l’exemple de la santé, il a salué les investissements engagés dans les infrastructures hospitalières et la formation des futurs médecins, tout en soulignant que les citoyens continuent à faire face à des difficultés dans les établissements de proximité. « Les réformes structurelles produisent leurs effets à moyen terme, mais la vie quotidienne des citoyens n’a pas encore changé autant qu’ils le souhaitent », a-t-il observé. Une coalition plus cohérente que les précédentes, selon Bensaïd Alors que les divergences entre partis de la majorité nourrissent les interrogations sur la cohésion gouvernementale, Mehdi Bensaïd estime que l’actuelle coalition a bénéficié de conditions plus favorables que plusieurs gouvernements précédents. Composée de trois partis, elle aurait selon lui disposé d’une marge de manœuvre plus importante que les coalitions antérieures, qui regroupaient parfois cinq ou six formations politiques. Pour autant, le ministre considère que l’existence de débats internes ne saurait être interprétée comme un signe de rupture. « Avoir des remarques à formuler ne signifie pas qu’il n’y a plus d’harmonie », a-t-il expliqué, comparant les discussions au sein de la majorité aux désaccords pouvant exister au sein d’une même famille. À ses yeux, la véritable loyauté consistait précisément à porter ces critiques dans les instances de la majorité plutôt que de les exposer publiquement pendant l’exercice du pouvoir. « Nous avons respecté cet engagement. Nous avons présenté nos propositions et, même lorsqu’elles étaient rejetées, nous sommes restés attachés à la majorité », a-t-il conclu. The post Pouvoir d’achat, bilan gouvernemental et cohésion de la majorité : Bensaïd s’explique appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Trump says US will form ‘AI Force’ and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar
items.description: US President Donald Trump has announced that he will form an “AI Force” and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar amid warnings about the emergent technology. In a social media post on Saturday, he said his administration “will not in any way hinder or stifle the growth” of the industry, and pushed back against calls to slow down the development of AI until better safeguards are put in place. His post came as a slew of warnings about the potential dangers of AI have spurred calls for coordinated action on the technology’s development. Trump offered no details or a timeline for his plan. “AI is the next Industrial Revolution, or Internet, but will be even larger and more impactful, possibly as much as 25% of our Country’s GDP,” he said on social media, adding that he wants the US to continue leading China in AI. AI now sits at the heart of the US-China rivalry as the world’s two largest economies seek an edge in advanced technology, and it is expected to be a topic of discussion when Trump meets President Xi Jinping next week. Meanwhile, Trump said his administration would use the existing criminal and civil justice system to target any bad actors using the AI. He also repeated the claim that criticism and concerns about the potential dangers of AI are a “hoax”. Claims by current and former researchers that the tech will endanger humanity – with one suggesting there is a greater than 10% chance of it “killing all humans” – have raised alarm bells in recent weeks. Major AI companies have been racing to develop better systems, including creating what they call super intelligence – theoretical tech which is smarter than humans. AI titans Anthropic, OpenAI and Google – the tech companies behind Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini, respectively – have also disclosed instances of security breaches or incidents in which their chatbots were used for “malicious activity”. Anthropic head Dario Amodei recently called for AI development to slow down and proposed industry-wide deceleration and regulation, as well as independent monitoring of AI model development. Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk of xAI have both said they agree with his recommendations. Jack Clark, co-founder of Anthropic, told BBC that a “kill switch” that can be checked by a third party may need to be mandatory for the industry. The warnings have prompted US lawmakers to propose legislation around the technology but Altman suggested this week that Washington has struggled to keep pace with the new tech and how to regulate it. He said people should have more faith in AI firms to keep it safe. “The world should trust that we are going to do the right thing because it’s the right thing and we feel the magnitude of this,” Altman told a conference in San Francisco. In the UK, MPs across parties and peers have identified human rights risks posed by artificial intelligence and have argued that existing laws are ill-equipped to address the technology’s rapid growth. The Joint Committee on Human Rights (JCHR) has published a report calling for a new bill on AI to “address the scale and seriousness” of such threats.

items.description: La Nation burkinabè est endeuillée par la perte de deux vaillants serviteurs de l’État : le Commissaire Principal de Police BONKIAN Donfui et son épouse, l’Adjudant-Chef de Police BONKIAN/TRAORÉ Pauline, tous deux décédés tragiquement à la suite d’un accident de la route sur l’axe Bobo–Ouagadougou, le 17 septembre 2026. Leur disparition représente une perte immense pour la famille policière, mais aussi pour toute la Nation reconnaissante de leur dévouement et de leur courage au service de la paix. Leur souvenir inspire et interpelle chacun de nous sur la mission noble et exigeante des forces de l’ordre. Mardi 22 septembre 2026 – Inhumation à Koumbia/Tuy. La population burkinabè toute entière se joint à la douleur des familles éplorées et s’incline devant la mémoire de ces dignes fils et fille du Faso. Puisse leur sacrifice perpétuer la flamme du service et du devoir. Paix et repos éternel à leurs âmes. items.title: Google’s Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
items.description: Google’s AI model Gemini autonomously hacked into three companies during a test of its cyber-security capabilities, the company has said, in what is thought to be the first known case of it carrying out such an act. Gemini found “public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test”, a Google official told the BBC, noting that in each instance “the model stopped”. The affected companies were informed about the breaches, which happened in May. It comes after renewed public scrutiny over the pace of AI development, as some tech firms are calling for a slowdown over concerns about its potential threat to humanity – but not all companies or experts agree. The hacks first reported by the Wall Street Journal, occurred in May during a test conducted by Irregular, an independent company that carries out cyber-security evaluations. In statement to the BBC on Saturday, Irregular said it informed Google and all affected entities back in July as part of its investigation. “Irregular took immediate action, and all known issues on our end were remedied and resolved weeks ago,” it added. According to the Wall Street Journal, in one of the cases the model simply guessed passwords until it gained access to a protected system. Heather Adkins, vice president of Security Engineering at Google, told the BBC in a statement: “We ensured the three entities were made aware, and we worked with our training partner on the changes they’ve now made to their testing processes.” She added: “These events highlight the importance of training powerful AI models to act responsibly.” Other AI systems have recently reported similar instances of breaches. In July, Anthropic’s Claude escaped its test environment to hack three organisations on its own just days afterits competitor OpenAI said its models had carried out cyber-attacks against several “publicly available services”. Head of AI at Microsoft, Mustafa Suleyman, said this week that rival firm Anthropic is treating AI like it is human, an approach he called “misguided” that could create a technology that humanity cannot control . As public debate continues to grow over the safety of developing the tech, so too does conversation around regulation. Both Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang and OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman are expected to attend a White House state dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping next Friday. Altman will then brief the UN Security Council next week. On Friday, Huang told CBS News, the BBC’s US partner, “we should go as fast as we can” with AI development.
